009540.KS.relative_comps: Cheapest on cash (P/FCF 3.2x, DCF MoS +67%, EPV +40%) against Korean yard peers that trade on rich backlog multiples. Growth is strong (rev +22%, EPS +85%) but margins are thin (gross 21%, net 7%) and the negative ROIC and Altman Z 1.8 flag a holding-company structure. Price sits near the 52-wk low and ~36% under the 200d, so the market is fading the shipbuilding upcycle. Discount looks partly real mispricing, partly a justified holdco/cyclical-peak haircut.
009540.KS.rationale: HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering (HD Hyundai group yard holding); the A&D industry tag is a screener mislabel. True comps are the Korean/Chinese/Japanese shipbuilders and offshore/naval builders.

0RG4.L.relative_comps: Unmapped: no reliable identification of this LSE 0R-prefix line, so no peer comparison is made. Data only: marine shipping profile, P/FCF 10.5x, net margin 43%, ROIC 12%, price above the 200d.
0RG4.L.rationale: unmapped: I do not recognise this ticker (0RG4.L is an LSE international-order-book style code) and the universe file has no company name. Do not propagate a guessed identity or peer multiple.

1308.HK.relative_comps: SITC trades at P/FCF 11x with ROIC 44% and net margin 36%, the best returns in the container-liner set, versus Evergreen/Yang Ming/Wan Hai at low single-digit to ~8x earnings through-cycle. The multi-method MoS is mixed (DCF +30%, owner earnings +27%, EPV ~-100%), so there is no clear mispricing. Price is just above the 200d and mid-range, so momentum is neutral. Premium to liners is justified by intra-Asia focus, consistent returns and a net-cash style balance sheet.
1308.HK.rationale: SITC International Holdings, intra-Asia container liner. Peers are listed container carriers; COSCO Shipping Holdings is in this universe, others are not.

1888.HK.relative_comps: Kingboard Laminates (copper-clad laminate maker). Gross margin 20% and net 12% sit below high-end AI laminate peers (Elite Material, Shengyi) but ROIC 13% and EPS +81% are solid. P/FCF is not usable (0.0 is a no-data default) and most MoS methods read -1, so valuation is unverified. Price is far off its 52-wk high (bottom ~17% of range, 35% under the 200d) after a spike and crash, which fits a fresh-crash flag rather than a clear discount.
1888.HK.rationale: Identified as Kingboard Laminates Holdings (PCB laminates), not a generic electrical-equipment name. Peers are PCB laminate makers in China/Taiwan/Korea.

1919.HK.relative_comps: COSCO Shipping Holdings is cheap on cash flow (P/FCF 10x) and on DCF (+52%), EPV (+46%) and owner earnings (+59%), but revenue is -6% and EPS -35% with a 3-yr revenue CAGR of -17%, i.e. earnings are rolling over from peak freight rates. Margins (gross 20%, net 14%) trail SITC but ROIC 19% is fine. Price is above the 200d and in the upper range, so the market already prices some of the discount away.
1919.HK.rationale: COSCO Shipping Holdings (China's state-owned liner plus terminals group). Peers are global container carriers; the earnings decline justifies part of the gap.

2618.HK.relative_comps: JD Logistics screens very cheap (P/FCF 5x, DCF +67%, owner earnings +62%, iv15 +74%) with strong revenue growth (+19%, 3y CAGR 16%). The cost is structure: gross margin 9%, net margin 3%, ROIC ~1%, well under SF Holding or ZTO unit economics, so the gap is mostly justified by low returns on an asset-heavy fulfilment model. Price is in the bottom ~11% of range and 18% under the 200d, which supports a mean-reversion case if margins improve.
2618.HK.rationale: JD Logistics (JD.com's logistics arm, HK listed). Peers are express and contract-logistics operators; most are not in this universe.

267260.KS.relative_comps: HD Hyundai Electric (transformers/switchgear) is expensive on cash flow (P/FCF 20.6x) and on most intrinsic methods (DCF -60%, EPV -100%), though growth is strong (rev +23%, EPS +46%) with gross margin 34% and net 18%. Hyosung Heavy and LS Electric trade on similar AI/grid-capex multiples, so the premium is a sector premium rather than a stock-specific one. Price is ~52% under its 200d and at the bottom of its range, so the market has already de-rated it hard.
267260.KS.rationale: HD Hyundai Electric, Korean power-equipment maker; peers are transformer and switchgear suppliers exposed to the grid/data-centre capex cycle.

5803.T.relative_comps: Fujikura (optical fibre and cable, AI data-centre exposure) is the richest in the set: P/FCF 51x and all intrinsic MoS methods at -100%, against Furukawa, Sumitomo Electric, Prysmian and Nexans at far lower multiples. Growth (rev +21%, EPS +72%) and margins (gross 28%, net 13%, ROIC 13%) are good but do not obviously justify the gap. Price is ~40% under the 200d and in the bottom 5% of range, so the AI-multiple has already compressed but still screens expensive.
5803.T.rationale: Fujikura Ltd. Peers are Japanese and European cable/fibre makers plus Corning; peer list excludes non-comparables.

9022.T.relative_comps: Central Japan Railway (Tokaido Shinkansen) has the best margins of the Japanese rail set (gross 52%, net 28%) but ROIC is only 3.8% because of the Chuo Shinkansen capex burden. P/FCF 17x is rich relative to JR East/West, and only the Graham MoS (+81%) flags value while DCF/EPV read -100%. Price is above the 200d in the upper range, so the market is not discounting it. Premium is justified by monopoly route quality, not by growth (rev +10%, EPS +23% on recovery).
9022.T.rationale: Central Japan Railway (JR Central). Peers are Japanese JR passenger railways and large private railways; no overseas rail operator has the same Shinkansen economics.

AEGN.AT.relative_comps: Aegean Airlines trades at P/FCF 12x with DCF +61%, owner earnings +65%, Graham +71%, a wide discount to its own intrinsic value. Growth is moderate (rev +5%, EPS +14%), margins net 8% / ROIC 6% sit in line with Wizz and Lufthansa and below Ryanair. Price is 5% under the 200d and in the lower range, with FCF down 68% y/y, so the cheapness is partly a cash-flow quality warning.
AEGN.AT.rationale: Aegean Airlines S.A. (Greece, Athens listing). Peers are European network/regional/low-cost airlines; seasonality and Greek tourism concentration justify some discount.

AGX.relative_comps: Argan (Gemma power EPC) trades at P/FCF 10.6x against 20-30x for Quanta, EMCOR, Comfort Systems and Sterling. Growth is strong (rev 3y CAGR 28%, EPS +58%) with ROIC 14%, but gross margin 20.5% and net 14.6% are project-driven and lumpy with very high customer concentration. Price is ~41% under the 200d and in the bottom 10% of range, so the market is discounting a peak-orders risk. The discount is partly deserved by backlog concentration but looks wide against the group.
AGX.rationale: Argan Inc. (Gemma Power Systems, gas-fired power plant EPC, plus industrial services). Peers are US specialty and utility contractors.

BRKN.SW.relative_comps: Burkhalter Holding (Swiss electrical installation). The 68% gross margin is an accounting artefact (labour is booked below gross), so use net margin 5% and ROIC 24%, which are good for the installer group (SPIE, Bravida, Instalco ROIC mostly 10-15%). P/FCF 14x and DCF +15% suggest modest value, with other methods at or below zero. Price is ~10% under the 200d and in the lower quarter of range.
BRKN.SW.rationale: Burkhalter Holding AG (Zurich), building-technology and electrical installation contractor, not a general E&C name. Peers are European installation/services contractors.

CKN.L.relative_comps: Clarkson (shipbroking and shipping services) trades at P/FCF 20x with DCF +31% but EPV -15% and other methods flat to negative, so it is fairly valued to slightly rich. Its gross margin of 93% reflects a fee-based model; net margin 10% and ROIC 14% are better than Braemar and in line with TP ICAP/Marex. Revenue is -5% and EPS -23% as freight volatility normalises. Price is at the 200d, mid-range, no momentum edge.
CKN.L.rationale: Clarkson PLC, the world's largest shipbroker. True peers are shipbrokers and inter-dealer brokers (Braemar, TP ICAP, Marex, BGC), not shipowners.

DAN.MI.relative_comps: Danieli (steel-plant builder with its own steel works) is cheap on cash (P/FCF 5.3x), DCF +56%, EPV +10%. Revenue is -9% and ROIC only 6% with Altman Z 1.4, which signals thin returns and weak balance-sheet quality, while the Andritz/Metso group trades at 12-20x earnings on steadier aftermarket mix. Price is 15% under the 200d, bottom third of range. The discount is mostly justified by cyclicality and steel-capex exposure, with a partial mispricing case via the cash flow and net-cash balance sheet.
DAN.MI.rationale: Danieli & C. Officine Meccaniche (Italy), metals-industry plant maker. Largest direct rivals SMS and Primetals are private, so listed comps are heavy-machinery proxies.

DUE.DE.relative_comps: Duerr (paint shops, final assembly, woodworking, clean-tech) screens very cheap: P/FCF 4.3x, DCF +65%, owner earnings +53%, Graham +84%. Margins are thin (gross 22%, net 4.9%, ROIC 5%) and revenue is -3% on weak auto capex, versus Krones/GEA at higher returns. Price is in the bottom ~7% of range and 14% under the 200d, so momentum is negative. A discount is justified by auto exposure and low returns, but the size of the gap argues for a real mispricing.
DUE.DE.rationale: Duerr AG (Bietigheim-Bissingen). Peers are German/European capital-goods automation and process-equipment makers, as no listed pure paint-shop competitor remains.

DY.relative_comps: Dycom (telecom/fibre construction) trades at P/FCF 16x with DCF and EPV reading -100%, i.e. not cheap versus MasTec or Primoris. Growth is good (rev +18%, EPS +21%) but net margin 5%, ROIC 9% and gross 21% are ordinary for contractors. Price is 40% under the 200d and in the bottom 10% of range, so the market already de-rated it. Fairly priced to rich on fundamentals; momentum is the only weak signal.
DY.rationale: Dycom Industries, US specialty contractor for telecom and fibre. Peers are US infrastructure contractors; customer concentration with a few carriers is the key risk.

EOLU-B.ST.relative_comps: Eolus Vind (Nordic wind developer and asset manager) shows P/FCF 0.7x and EPV +38% but the data are noisy: revenue +360% and zero gross margin reflect lumpy project sales. Net margin is -9% and ROIC 4%, versus Arise and Scatec on steadier cash flow. Price is in the upper range and above the 200d, so some re-rating has already occurred. Valuation signals are unreliable because of project timing.
EOLU-B.ST.rationale: Eolus Vind AB (Sweden), wind-farm developer. Peers are small/mid-cap renewable developers and IPPs, not turbine makers.

FAG.ST.relative_comps: Fagerhult (professional lighting) is cheap on cash (P/FCF 4.6x) and on all main methods (DCF +70%, EPV +53%, owner earnings +74%), against Zumtobel and Signify at 8-12x FCF. Revenue is -5%, EPS -10%, net margin 4% and ROIC 4.5% versus Acuity's high-teens returns, so quality is lower. Price is at its 52-wk low and 42% under the 200d. The discount is partly justified by shrinking sales and weak ROIC, but the gap to European lighting peers is large.
FAG.ST.rationale: Fagerhult Group AB (Sweden), commercial lighting. Peers are lighting and building-technology companies in Europe and North America.

FGR.PA.relative_comps: Eiffage is cheap on every method (P/FCF 3.6x, DCF +71%, EPV +42%, owner earnings +66%, iv15 +56%) with moderate growth (rev +9%, 3y CAGR 8%). Margins (gross 13%, net 3.9%) and ROIC 6% match European contractors, but its motorway concession mix gives better cash visibility than Bouygues or Skanska. Price is 11% under the 200d, lower range. Altman Z of 1.0 reflects concession debt, so the discount is only partly justified.
FGR.PA.rationale: Eiffage SA (France): construction plus motorway concessions (APRR). Peers are large European builder-concessionaires, Vinci being the nearest.

GHC.relative_comps: Graham Holdings (Kaplan education, TV, healthcare, manufacturing, auto dealerships) has P/FCF 19.8x, with only Graham (+79%) and owner earnings (+24%) flagging value, while DCF and EPV are negative. Growth is weak (rev +2.5%, EPS -59%) and ROIC 1.5% is low, versus Adtalem/Strategic Education at far higher education-segment returns. Price is near its 52-wk high and above the 200d. Valuation sits above diversified holding peers, not obviously justified by its earnings trend.
GHC.rationale: Graham Holdings Co., a diversified holding company. Peers are diversified holdcos (Loews, Seaboard, Steel Partners, Icahn) plus listed education and broadcast operators for the segments.

HUBG.relative_comps: Hub Group is an intermodal/asset-light truckload and logistics broker; P/FCF about 10.5 with a screener multi-method MoS spread of roughly 28-56% on DCF/EPV/owner earnings. Revenue is -6% y/y and EPS -35%, with net margin about 2.6% and ROIC about 8%, so it is cheap on cash flow but earning thin freight-cycle returns versus JBHT/LSTR, which carry higher ROIC and richer multiples. Price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range and well below the 200-day average, so momentum is poor. The discount is largely justified by the freight downturn and margin compression, but the gap to intermodal leaders looks wide enough to be partly a cyclical-trough mispricing. The reported 85% gross margin is a net-revenue accounting artifact, so ignore it.
HUBG.rationale: US intermodal and logistics operator (Hub Group); peers are other intermodal carriers, truckload brokers and asset-light 3PLs.

HUSQ-B.ST.relative_comps: Husqvarna (outdoor power products: chainsaws, mowers, robotic mowers; Gardena irrigation) trades at P/FCF about 9.7 with mixed method MoS (DCF +50%, EPV -22%, so the cheapness is not corroborated). Revenue -3.6% y/y and ROIC about 7% with a 3.8% net margin are weak versus Toro (higher ROIC, premium multiple) and Techtronic (best-in-class growth and margins). Altman Z about 1.6 and a leveraged balance sheet add risk. Stanley Black and Decker is the closest same-shaped, similarly depressed peer. The discount to Toro/Techtronic is mostly justified by lower returns and cyclical consumer exposure; modest cheapness only versus Stanley B&D-type turnarounds.
HUSQ-B.ST.rationale: Husqvarna Group (Swedish outdoor power equipment and garden tools); peers are Toro, Stanley Black and Decker, Techtronic, Makita, Deere (turf).

IAG.L.relative_comps: IAG (BA, Iberia, Vueling, Aer Lingus) trades at P/FCF about 8.8 with DCF/owner-earnings MoS of +42-47%, in line with the low multiples of European network carriers (Air France-KLM, Lufthansa) but with better net margin (10%) and returns than both. Revenue is nearly flat y/y with EPS +25%; ROIC about 6.7% is modest and Altman Z about 1.7 reflects airline leverage. Price is in the upper part of its 52-week range, above its 200-day average, so momentum is positive. Premium to AF-KLM and Lufthansa is justified by superior margins and transatlantic mix; versus US majors it screens cheap.
IAG.L.rationale: International Consolidated Airlines Group (British Airways parent); peers are European network carriers plus low-cost and US majors.

JUN3.DE.relative_comps: Jungheinrich (preferred shares; forklifts, warehouse automation, leasing) shows P/FCF about 6.6 and strong multi-method MoS (DCF +60%, EPV +62%, owner earnings +72%), the cheapest profile in its group. Revenue +2%, but EPS -64% and a net margin of about 1.9% show margin compression; ROIC about 5.8% is low. Peers KION (similar cyclical margin trough, also leveraged) and Toyota Industries (higher quality, richer) bracket it. Price is near the low end of its 52-week range and below the 200-day average. The discount versus Toyota Industries is partly justified by lower returns, but the earnings trough looks cyclical and the gap is large, so it screens as a genuine mispricing candidate if intralogistics demand recovers.
JUN3.DE.rationale: Jungheinrich AG (Hamburg, forklift trucks and intralogistics); peers are KION/Linde MH, Toyota Industries (Raymond), Hyster-Yale and Cargotec/Kalmar.

LIGHT.AS.relative_comps: Signify (Philips Lighting; global leader in LED and connected lighting) trades at P/FCF about 4.9 with high MoS across DCF (+66%), owner earnings (+65%) and EPV (+47%). Revenue is -6% y/y (three-year CAGR -8%), EPS -21%, net margin 4.4%, ROIC about 7%, so it is a structurally shrinking, price-deflating business versus Acuity Brands (higher margins, US non-residential, premium multiple) and Legrand (higher quality). Altman Z about 1.2 is a flag. Price is near the lows. The discount is largely justified by LED commoditisation and negative growth, but the FCF yield is high enough that some of the gap looks like a real mispricing if conversions stabilise.
LIGHT.AS.rationale: Signify N.V. (Eindhoven, lighting); peers are Acuity Brands, Zumtobel, Fagerhult, Hubbell/Legrand electrical exposure.

MBB.DE.relative_comps: MBB SE is a German listed holding that owns industrial and tech businesses (e.g. Aumann, Friedrich Vorwerk, Polytec, DTS), so it is valued on a sum-of-the-parts basis against other small-cap holding companies. P/FCF about 5.9 and DCF/IV15 MoS of about 44-55% are cheap, though owner-earnings and EPV are mixed. Revenue +9.5% y/y, EPS +37%, but net margin about 4% and ROIC about 3.7% are low; Altman Z 2.7 is fine. Price is in the upper-middle of its 52-week range, above the 200-day average, so momentum is constructive. Discount to NAV versus Indus Holding and Mutares is typical of the holding-company structure; growth and trend are better than most peers, so the gap looks partly a mispricing.
MBB.DE.rationale: MBB SE (Berlin) is a German Mittelstand holding company; peers are other listed industrial holdings and buy-and-build vehicles.

MGNS.L.relative_comps: Morgan Sindall (UK construction, fit-out, infrastructure, property partnerships and urban regeneration) trades at P/FCF about 11.7 with DCF MoS +28% and owner earnings +16% but negative EPV, so cheapness is moderate rather than deep. Growth is strong (revenue +10%, EPS +31%) and ROIC about 14% is the best in the UK contractor peer group, while the 3.5% net margin is typical of the sector. Altman Z 3.7 shows a clean balance sheet. Price is in the lower-middle of its range and below the 200-day average. A modest premium to Kier, Galliford Try and Costain is justified by better returns and growth, so it screens in line to modestly rich on cash flow.
MGNS.L.rationale: Morgan Sindall Group plc (UK contractor); peers are Balfour Beatty, Kier, Galliford Try, Costain, Keller.

MNC.WA.relative_comps: Mennica Polska (Warsaw; precious-metals trading and processing, mint and jewellery business) has limited recognizable listed comparables, so the peer set is partial (A-Mark is the closest listed trading/minting analogue; Umicore and Johnson Matthey are only adjacent recycling and refining models). P/FCF about 6.7 with graham MoS +85% and owner earnings +43% but EPV -100% and DCF +11%, so the methods disagree. Revenue +31% and an EPS jump of 5.4x with an unusually high 27% net margin look driven by one-off or metal-price effects, not run-rate economics. Gross margin about 11% fits the metals-trading model. Price is in the lower part of its range. The apparent cheapness is not reliable; it is not clearly mispriced.
MNC.WA.rationale: Mennica Polska S.A. (Warsaw-listed precious-metals trader and mint); thin real peer set, reasoned from business model, moderate confidence.

MPCC.OL.relative_comps: MPC Container Ships (feeder container vessel owner) trades at P/FCF about 7.3, with DCF and owner-earnings MoS of about 38-40% but EPV -49%, so earnings power versus peak rates is a concern. Peers Danaos, Global Ship Lease and Costamare trade at similar or lower multiples with comparable, charter-backed cashflows. Revenue is -4% y/y (three-year CAGR -8%) as rates normalise, but net margin of 46% and ROIC about 31% are exceptional, in line with container lessors at cycle highs. Price is in the upper half of its range. The market is pricing normalised charter rates, so the valuation is in line with the peer set and cyclical risk is the justification.
MPCC.OL.rationale: MPC Container Ships ASA (Oslo-listed feeder container ship owner); peers are listed container tonnage owners and liner operators.

MULTI.OL.relative_comps: Multiconsult is a Norwegian engineering and design consultancy; P/FCF about 21.6 is rich versus Sweco, Afry and Norconsult, and multi-method MoS is mixed (owner earnings +61%, DCF +28%, EPV -12%). Revenue +4% (three-year CAGR +11%) but EPS -39%, net margin about 3.8% and ROIC about 14% are respectable for consulting, though not better than Sweco. Price is in the lower part of its range and below its 200-day average. The premium to Nordic peers is not backed by superior growth, and the 85% gross margin is a net-revenue accounting artifact. Quality is fine but the multiple looks full relative to the EPS decline.
MULTI.OL.rationale: Multiconsult ASA (Oslo-listed Norwegian engineering consultancy); peers are Sweco, Afry, Norconsult, Rejlers, Arcadis.

NAS.OL.relative_comps: Norwegian Air Shuttle (Nordic low-cost airline) trades at P/FCF about 7.7 with very high multi-method MoS (DCF +78%, owner earnings +82%, graham +89%), the cheapest profile among European airlines. Revenue +3.5% (three-year CAGR +25%) and EPS +107% show strong recovery, with net margin 7.4%, but ROIC is only about 0.4% on the screener and Altman Z about 1.3 reflects a leveraged post-restructuring balance sheet. Price is in the lower-middle of its range and below its 200-day average. Versus Ryanair and easyJet it is cheap, but Ryanair's superior cost base and balance sheet justify a premium, so part of the gap is justified by quality; the rest looks like a real mispricing.
NAS.OL.rationale: Norwegian Air Shuttle ASA (Oslo-listed Nordic low-cost airline); peers are European low-cost and network carriers.

NRC.OL.relative_comps: NRC Group (Norwegian-Swedish rail infrastructure services and contractor) is rich on P/FCF at about 24.2 with deeply negative MoS across methods (DCF -67%, EPV/graham/owner earnings at -100%), negative ROIC (-6%) and Altman Z of 1.9. Revenue is -5% and net margin near zero. Peers such as Balfour Beatty, Kier and Costain generate positive ROIC and trade at lower multiples on cash flow. The stock is in the lower-middle of its range. The 97% gross margin is a net-revenue accounting artifact, not real. The premium is not justified by growth or returns, so it looks expensive relative to the peer set.
NRC.OL.rationale: NRC Group ASA (Oslo-listed Nordic railway infrastructure contractor); peers are listed civil, rail and infrastructure contractors.

ODF.OL.relative_comps: Odfjell (chemical and specialty tankers, with terminals) trades at P/FCF about 5.0 with strong multi-method MoS (DCF +71%, owner earnings +78%, EPV +51%). Revenue -11% y/y and EPS -44% reflect softer rates, but net margin 14% and ROIC about 12% remain solid. Stolt-Nielsen, the closest peer, trades at a comparable multiple with a more diversified model; product tanker owners (Torm, Hafnia, Ardmore) trade on similar low FCF multiples. Price is in the lower-middle of its range and below its 200-day average. The discount reflects falling rates and cyclicality, but the FCF yield and returns suggest a modest underpricing.
ODF.OL.rationale: Odfjell SE (Oslo-listed chemical tanker owner); peers are Stolt-Nielsen and listed product and chemical tanker owners.

Pluxee (PLX.PA) and Edenred (EDEN.PA) are the employee-benefits/voucher near-duopoly and BOTH de-rated on the SAME regulatory shock - the Brazil PAT reform + Italy voucher cap (Kepler cut PLX EUR28->EUR18 and EDEN EUR40->EUR28 on the same event). Edenred now trades ~10x fwd P/E / ~4x EV/2026e EBITDA, NOT its pre-shock 20-25x. Pluxee at ~5x P/FCF vs a ~10x Edenred is a MODEST discount, largely justified by Pluxee's heavier Brazil concentration (guided ~50% Brazil revenue drop; Edenred took an 8-12% group EBITDA hit on the same reforms). The convergence is SECTOR-REGULATORY BETA on a shared, unresolved factor - NOT idiosyncratic single-name alpha - which is exactly what a correlation-stressed apex basket is built to discount.

RENT3.SA.relative_comps: Localiza (Brazil's largest car rental and fleet-leasing group) trades at P/FCF about 11.1 with mixed MoS (EPV +47%, owner earnings +66%, DCF -100%), so the signal is not clean for an asset-heavy leasing business. Revenue +12% (three-year CAGR +33% after the Unidas merger), EPS +4%, net margin 4.5% and ROIC about 7.6% are modest in a high-rate Brazil. Altman Z about 1.3 reflects leverage typical of fleet financing. Price is in the lower part of its range and well below its 200-day average. Versus Movida it is the quality leader, while against Hertz and Avis it is less cyclical but exposed to Brazilian rates and currency. The multiple looks in line with a rate-sensitive leasing model.
RENT3.SA.rationale: Localiza&Co (Brazil, car rental and fleet management); peers are Movida, Hertz, Avis Budget, Sixt, Ryder.

RHM.DE.relative_comps: Rheinmetall (German land systems, ammunition and defense electronics) is rich on P/FCF at about 25.3; the screener flags -100% MoS on DCF, EPV, graham and owner earnings. SMIN.L.relative_comps: Smiths Group (John Crane seals and flow, Flex-Tek, Smiths Interconnect; after divesting parts of the portfolio) is rich on P/FCF at about 47.8 with negative DCF and EPV MoS (-41% and -71%). Price is in the upper part of its range, above its 200-day average. The premium is not supported by clean growth or returns, so it screens rich versus the UK industrial-engineering peer set.
SMIN.L.rationale: Smiths Group plc (UK, flow control, interconnect and thermal products); peers are Spirax, IMI, Weir, Halma, Crane, ITT.

The cheapness reflects cyclical rate risk and a still-thin earnings history, but the gap is large enough to look partly real.
SOFF.OL.rationale: Solstad Offshore ASA (Oslo-listed offshore support vessel owner); peers are Tidewater, DOF, Seacor Marine, Eidesvik.

STRL.rationale: Sterling Infrastructure Inc. (US site development and infrastructure contractor); peers are listed US infrastructure and specialty contractors.

TEP.PA.relative_comps: Teleperformance (global customer-experience and BPO outsourcing leader) trades at P/FCF about 3.7 with high multi-method MoS (DCF +72%, owner earnings +71%, EPV +49%), the lowest multiple in the CX/BPO group. The discount is attributable to AI-displacement risk to call-centre volumes and slowing growth, which is a real thesis, but the gap to peers is large and looks only partly justified.
TEP.PA.rationale: Teleperformance SE (Paris-listed contact-centre and BPO outsourcer); peers are Concentrix, Genpact, TaskUs, TTEC, Conduent.

0135.HK.relative_comps: Kunlun Energy (CNPC unit: gas distribution, LNG processing, plus legacy oil and gas E&P stakes) screens at p_fcf 7.6 and EPV/DCF MoS ~56%, well below Chinese city-gas peers that usually trade at 10-15x FCF. Cheap, but the state-parent related-party structure and thin margins justify part of the gap.
0135.HK.rationale: Kunlun Energy (CNPC subsidiary) is mainly a PRC gas-distribution and LNG operator, so the real comps are the HK-listed city-gas utilities, not oil refiners; the FMP industry tag is misleading.

1605.T.relative_comps: INPEX (Japan's largest E&P; Ichthys LNG, Abadi) trades at p_fcf 6.3x with EPV MoS 52% and owner-earnings MoS 39%, cheap versus Woodside/Santos/ConocoPhillips at roughly 8-12x FCF. Revenue -11% y/y and ROIC 5% are weak, and Graham-style MoS is negative, so the cheapness reflects falling output/price and a heavy asset base plus Japan-government golden share. Price is in the lower-middle of its range (0.32). Modest real discount, partly justified.
1605.T.rationale: INPEX Corp is a pure upstream and LNG developer with global assets, so large LNG-weighted independents and mid-cap E&Ps are the right set.

1898.HK.relative_comps: China Coal Energy trades at p_fcf 13.9x, higher than its H-share thermal-coal peers (Yankuang, Shenhua usually 6-10x), though EPV/DCF MoS (56-64%) look big. Revenue -21% and EPS -22% are the worst growth in the set, and the stock sits near its 52-week low (proximity 0.10, well under SMA200). Margins (net 9.8%, ROIC 11%) are in line with peers. Looks optically cheap on intrinsic value but not on FCF, and the trend is down; trade it as in-line to rich on cash flow.
1898.HK.rationale: China Coal Energy is a PRC thermal and coking coal miner plus coal-chemical, so Chinese coal producers and seaborne thermal producers are the real peers.

AKRBP.OL.relative_comps: Aker BP (Norwegian NCS pure-play E&P, Johan Sverdrup stake) screens with EPV MoS only 25% and negative DCF/Graham/owner-earnings MoS, so it is the least discounted of the Norwegian E&Ps despite best-in-class cost and margins (gross 65%). p_fcf is 0 (negative or unavailable FCF from heavy capex), EPS -93% y/y, ROIC 4%, Altman Z 1.1. BTU.relative_comps: Peabody (thermal plus met coal, US and Australia) shows EPV MoS 45% and owner-earnings MoS 61%, but p_fcf is 0 (FCF negative or missing), net margin -1.4%, gross 2.7% and revenue -9%. It trades near its 52-week low (0.07, below SMA200) like most US coal. Versus Core Natural Resources/ARLP it carries lower margins and weaker FCF, so the apparent MoS discount is largely justified by earnings quality and thermal-coal terminal risk.
BTU.rationale: Peabody is a US and Australian thermal and metallurgical coal producer, so US-listed coal miners and seaborne coal names are the peers.

DMLP.relative_comps: Dorchester Minerals (unlevered oil and gas mineral/royalty partnership) trades at p_fcf 10.3x with DCF MoS 58% and owner-earnings MoS 53%, but EPV MoS is -86%. Margins are royalty-class (gross 46%, net 38%, ROIC 46%, Altman Z 81, no debt) which beat BSM/KRP/VNOM on balance sheet cleanliness. Growth is weak (rev -5%, EPS -44%) and price is near the upper range (0.77). In-line with mineral peers on yield-adjusted cash flow; the unlevered quality justifies a premium, so the discount is not large.
DMLP.rationale: Dorchester Minerals is a US mineral and royalty interest owner, so the listed US mineral/royalty vehicles are the real comps, not E&P operators.

DOFG.OL.relative_comps: DOF Group (subsea and offshore vessel and project services) trades at p_fcf 13.4x with EPV MoS 67% and owner-earnings MoS 92%, but Graham negative. Growth is strong (rev +35% y/y, EPS +103%) with solid margins (gross 67%, net 25%, Altman Z 10) and price near highs (0.69, 52w up). Valuation versus Subsea7/TDW/Oceaneering is roughly in line on FCF, while model MoS flags upside; momentum and cycle upswing explain it, so the mispricing signal is modest.
DOFG.OL.rationale: DOF Group ASA is a Norwegian subsea vessel owner and offshore subsea project contractor, so offshore vessel operators and subsea contractors are the peers.

ENPH.relative_comps: Enphase (microinverters and storage) trades at p_fcf 36.7x, rich versus a depressed solar group and versus FSLR/SEDG on FCF, with EPV MoS -67% and Graham -100% (only DCF 55% and owner earnings 30% positive). Revenue +11% and EPS +72% off a trough, gross margin 47% and ROIC 9.7% are best-in-class among inverter makers, but the stock sits at the 52-week low (0.04, far under SMA200) as residential-solar demand and the US tax-credit roll-off weigh. Premium valuation is partly justified by margin quality, but the tape and declining demand argue it is not cheap.
ENPH.rationale: Enphase is a residential solar and storage electronics supplier, so solar inverter and residential solar/storage names are the peers, not oil and gas.

EQNR.OL.relative_comps: Equinor (Norwegian state-controlled integrated, gas and offshore wind) trades at p_fcf 18x, higher than Shell/Total/Eni at ~8-12x because heavy capex and a large Norwegian tax burden depress FCF; EPV MoS 51% but DCF 22% and Graham -73%. Revenue +13% but EPS -32%; ROIC 10.7% and net margin 4.8% are in line with majors. Price is near the upper range (0.79). Mildly rich on FCF versus European majors, with the premium resting on gas security and the dividend.
EQNR.OL.rationale: Equinor ASA is a Norwegian integrated oil and gas major with offshore wind, so European integrated majors are the right set.

HBR.L.relative_comps: Harbour Energy (North Sea E&P, big after the Wintershall Dea upstream deal) shows p_fcf 3.3x and EPV MoS 79%, the cheapest FCF multiple in the group, with DCF 62% and owner-earnings 65% also high. Revenue +66% reflects the acquisition, but quality is poor: net margin -1.8%, ROIC 0.4%, Altman Z 0.89, heavy debt and UK windfall tax. Price is mid-upper range (0.61). The discount to Aker BP/Var is large but largely explained by leverage, UK fiscal regime and distress risk, so it is cheap with real risk rather than a pure mispricing.
HBR.L.rationale: Harbour Energy plc is a UK-listed North Sea E&P now with international assets, so UK and Norwegian North Sea producers are the peers.

IEP.relative_comps: Icahn Enterprises is a diversified holding company (Investment funds, CVR refining and nitrogen fertilizer, auto, food packaging, real estate); the Energy tag is only its largest segment. Net margin -3.1%, ROIC about 0%, Altman Z 1.3, and it trades near its 52-week low (0.04). p_fcf is 0 (FCF negative). DCF MoS 80% is not credible given negative earnings and a leveraged structure. Versus conglomerates/holdcos it trades at a persistent discount to NAV, which is justified by the high-yield dividend funded by debt and fund losses; the apparent cheapness is not a clear mispricing.
IEP.rationale: IEP is a diversified holding company whose value is driven by Icahn's investment funds and CVR Energy, so holdcos and the CVR refiner peers are the correct comparison, not an oil refiner alone.

LBRT.relative_comps: Liberty Energy (US frac and completions, expanding into power generation) shows p_fcf 154x because FCF is near zero after heavy growth capex, EPV MoS -72% and DCF only 3%, so it is rich on cash flow versus Halliburton/Patterson/RPC. Revenue -7%, EPS -52%, gross margin 11%, net margin 3.7%, ROIC 10%. The stock is near its 52-week low (0.08) but well above its low point at 11. Rich on FCF; the premium is a bet on the power-generation pivot rather than on frac economics.
LBRT.rationale: Liberty Energy is a US pressure-pumping/fracking services provider with a growing distributed-power business, so frac and OFS peers are the comps.

LEU.relative_comps: Centrus Energy (LEU enrichment and HALEU, SWU trading) trades at p_fcf 66x with negative DCF/EPV/Graham MoS (-62%/-80%/-46%), rich versus Cameco and fuel-cycle peers on all value methods. Growth is modest (rev +1.5%, 3y CAGR 15%, EPS -13%), though margins and ROIC are healthy (gross 26%, net 17%, ROIC 15%). The stock is at the lows of its range (0.07 proximity, far under SMA200) after a huge run to a $345 high. Premium reflects scarcity (the only US-owned enrichment supplier) and HALEU optionality, so the premium is partly justified but not by current earnings.
LEU.rationale: Centrus Energy is a nuclear fuel supplier (enrichment SWU, LEU and HALEU), so the nuclear fuel cycle names are the peers, not oil and gas.

MAU.PA.relative_comps: Maurel & Prom (Africa and Latin America E&P, Gabon, Tanzania, Angola, Colombia; Indonesia's Pertamina-linked stake) shows blended MoS: Graham 85%, owner-earnings 60%, EPV -12% and DCF -3%, and p_fcf 0 (FCF not meaningful). Revenue -26% but EPS +82%, net margin 71% is distorted by a one-off gain. The stock trades mid-low range (0.37). Method disagreement and a one-off-driven net margin mean there is no clear mispricing against Seplat/VAALCO/Kosmos; in line.
MAU.PA.rationale: Maurel & Prom is a Paris-listed E&P with Gabon, Tanzania, Angola and Colombia assets, so emerging-market and West African-focused E&Ps are the peers.

NOG.relative_comps: Northern Oil & Gas (non-operated Bakken/Permian working interests) trades at p_fcf 9.9x, in line with shale E&Ps of 6-10x, with only Graham MoS 14% positive and DCF/EPV at -100%. Revenue -3% and EPS -92% (impairment), net margin 1.9% and Altman Z 0.46 show high leverage. The stock is mid-range (0.57) and ROIC 17%. Valuation is in line to slightly rich once leverage and the non-operated model are accounted for.
NOG.rationale: Northern Oil and Gas is a US non-operated shale working-interest company, so Bakken and Permian E&Ps are the peers.

OKEA.OL.relative_comps: OKEA (Norwegian mid-cap NCS producer; Brage, Draugen, Gjoa) displays model MoS of 95% (capped) on DCF/EPV/owner earnings and 84% on deep-value, but the data is unreliable: revenue -93% and 3y CAGR -50% look like a restatement, p_fcf is 0 and net margin -7%. The stock is near its 52-week high (0.86). Cheap on paper versus Aker BP/Var, yet the capped 95% MoS and corrupted growth fields mean confidence should be low; leverage and bond financing add risk.
OKEA.OL.rationale: OKEA ASA is a Norwegian continental-shelf oil and gas producer, so NCS and North Sea mid-cap E&Ps are the peers.

PBT.relative_comps: Permian Basin Royalty Trust (net profits interest in Waddell Ranch plus Texas Royalty properties) is a pass-through with no debt; margins are the trust's accounting (gross 100%, net 89%, ROIC not meaningful), revenue -41%, EPS -44%, and p_fcf 0 (not meaningful for a trust). EPV MoS 17% and others negative, and the stock sits upper-mid range (0.71). Depleting royalty trusts should trade below perpetual mineral owners like Dorchester; on a yield basis it is in line with Sabine/SJT, so there is no clear mispricing.
PBT.rationale: PBT is a US royalty trust (net profits interest), so other royalty trusts and mineral owners are the peers; it is not an operating company.

PETR3.SA.relative_comps: Petrobras (common shares, ON) trades at p_fcf 7.3x with DCF MoS 67% and EPV MoS 31%, cheap versus European integrated majors and in line with state-owned peers like Ecopetrol. Margins are strong (gross 44%, net 22%, ROIC 15%), EPS +201% y/y on a low base; price is mid-range (0.59). The discount reflects political and governance risk (dividend policy, state intervention), so it is cheap but with a justified risk premium.
PETR3.SA.rationale: PETR3.SA is the common (ON) share of Petrobras, the Brazilian state-controlled integrated oil major, so integrated majors and state-owned NOCs are the right peers.

PNOR.OL.relative_comps: PetroNor E&P (Oslo small-cap with Congo/Nigeria assets and the Hemla/ Sao Tome/West Africa portfolio) trades at p_fcf 3.6x with DCF 74% and EPV 72% MoS, cheap versus Panoro and VAALCO. Margins are decent (gross 59%, net 9%, ROIC 18%) but revenue -58% and EPS -79% show a sharp decline and large volatility. The stock sits near the lower range (0.14). The discount reflects small size, single-asset concentration and country risk, so it is cheap but not a clear mispricing.
PNOR.OL.rationale: PetroNor E&P is an Oslo-listed small-cap West Africa E&P (Congo-Brazzaville focus), so small West African producers such as Panoro and VAALCO are the peers.

SEA1.OL.relative_comps: Cheap on the screen: p_fcf of about 9.5 sits below Tidewater and DOF, and the MoS methods are high (epv 0.35, dcf 0.66, graham 0.77). Growth is the weak spot: revenue -18% y/y and eps -14% while the offshore support-vessel cycle is firm. The 42% net margin looks inflated by gains, vessel sales or tax rather than recurring earnings. Price is only about 32% up the 52-week range and sits under its sma200, so trend is weak. The discount to Tidewater and Solstad is partly justified by shrinking revenue, Altman z of 1.8 and a smaller fleet; call it cheap but not a clean mispricing until the net margin is normalised.
SEA1.OL.rationale: Sea1 Offshore ASA (formerly Siem Offshore), Oslo-listed owner of offshore support vessels (PSV, AHTS, subsea/CSV). The real comps are the other OSV owners: Tidewater, Solstad Offshore, DOF Group, SEACOR Marine, Eidesvik and Hornbeck. Not drillers or oilfield-service equipment names, despite the FMP industry tag.

VAL.relative_comps: Mixed valuation signal: Graham MoS is very high (0.87), but DCF, EPV and iv15 all read -1.0 (no intrinsic value after capex), and p_fcf of about 29 is rich against offshore-driller peers. Price is mid-range at roughly 55% of the 52-week range and below its sma200. Against Transocean, Noble, Seadrill and Borr, Valaris has the stronger balance sheet and floater/jackup mix, which supports a premium, but the screen's FCF multiple leaves little room. Treat it as in line to rich on cash flow, not a bargain.
VAL.rationale: Valaris Ltd, the offshore contract driller (floaters and jackups). The true peers are Transocean, Noble, Seadrill and Borr Drilling; Helmerich & Payne and Precision Drilling are secondary land-drilling comps.

WFRD.relative_comps: Valuation: p_fcf of about 13.9 is in line to slightly cheap against SLB and Halliburton (roughly 12-18x FCF). The MoS spread is moderate (dcf 0.25, owner earnings 0.33, graham 0.70, epv near zero), so the market already prices most of the cash flow. Growth is negative (revenue -11% y/y, eps -12%) in a softer oilfield-services cycle. Margins are the weak point: gross 22% and net 8.8% sit below the large caps, though roic_avg of 13% is solid. Price is about 40% up the 52-week range and under its sma200, so momentum is weak. The discount to SLB is justified by lower margins and scale; the stock reads as fair rather than mispriced.
WFRD.rationale: Weatherford International, a mid-cap global oilfield-services provider (well construction, completions, production, MPD). The true peers are the diversified service majors (SLB, Halliburton, Baker Hughes) plus NOV, TechnipFMC, Expro and Oceaneering.

1339.HK.relative_comps: PICC Group (P&C, life and bank holdco) screens extremely cheap on the model MoS spread (DCF/Graham ~0.84, EPV 0.40) but p_fcf 1.4 and gross_margin 1.10 are insurer-cash-flow artifacts, so ignore p_fcf. Growth is steady (rev +8%, eps +10%) with thin ROIC 3.5%, and price sits near the low of its 52-wk range (13% position). The discount to Chinese insurer peers is mostly a holdco/state-ownership and P&C-underwriting-quality discount, partly justified, but the depth of discount to book is a plausible mispricing.
1339.HK.rationale: PICC Group Co (1339.HK, H-shares) per sector=Insurance P&C; real peers are PICC P&C (2328.HK), Ping An, CPIC, China Life and the Chinese composite insurers.

1988.HK.relative_comps: China Minsheng Banking is a small-cap joint-stock bank with shrinking revenue (-8%) and eps (-10%) and ROIC 1.6%, below the large state banks. Multi-method MoS is high (EPV 0.36, Graham 0.51, owner earnings 0.68) but DCF/iv15 are invalid for a bank, so lean on P/B. Trading at 13% of 52-wk range, below its sma200, it is cheap vs. large Chinese banks on book but deserves the discount given weaker asset quality and negative growth; justified more than mispriced.
1988.HK.rationale: China Minsheng Banking Corp (1988.HK H-share), a Chinese joint-stock commercial bank; peers are China Merchants Bank, CITIC Bank, Bank of Communications, Everbright, ICBC.

2601.HK.relative_comps: CPIC H-share is a life and P&C composite with eps +16% on revenue -6%, ROIC 1.5%, and trades near the bottom of its 52-wk range (11% position) well below sma200. The model's EPV MoS is slim (0.08) while DCF/Graham are very high, a wide spread that signals model disagreement, not clean cheapness. Versus Ping An and China Life it is a quality composite with stronger agent-channel reform narrative, so a modest discount looks mostly in line.
2601.HK.rationale: China Pacific Insurance (Group) 2601.HK, the H-share of CPIC; direct peers are Ping An, China Life, PICC, NCI and AIA.

2628.HK.relative_comps: China Life (H) shows the strongest growth in the group (rev +18%, eps +44%, net margin 25%) yet trades near the bottom of its 52-wk range (7% position) and below sma200. EPV MoS 0.46 and DCF 0.91 are the highest among insurers in the batch; p_fcf is not meaningful. Earnings are volatile because they ride equity-market gains, and ROIC is only 5%, so part of the discount reflects earnings quality, but the gap to growth is large enough to look like genuine mispricing.
2628.HK.rationale: China Life Insurance Co (2628.HK), largest Chinese life insurer; peers are Ping An, CPIC, New China Life, PICC, AIA and Prudential.

8725.T.relative_comps: MS&AD is a Japanese megainsurer with solid growth (rev +13%, eps +19%), ROIC 11.6% and p_fcf of 10.8, the best fundamentals of the P&C names in the batch. It sits at 98% of its 52-wk range and above sma200, so momentum is strong and the multi-method MoS (0.28-0.47) is positive but not extreme. Against Tokio Marine and Sompo it is in line to slightly cheap; the re-rating (cross-shareholding unwind, buybacks) is already largely visible in price.
8725.T.rationale: MS&AD Insurance Group Holdings (8725.T), Japan's second/third largest non-life group; peers are Tokio Marine, Sompo, plus global P&C Chubb, Travelers, Allianz, Zurich.

AJB.L.relative_comps: AJ Bell is a UK investment platform with strong growth (rev +18%, 3y CAGR +25%, eps +30%), net margin 33% and ROIC 40%. It is expensive on p_fcf (28x) and the model MoS spread is negative (EPV -1.0, DCF -0.10), so valuation is rich vs. UK/US brokers, though quality is the best of the group. Trading at 63% of its 52-wk range and above sma200. Premium is partly justified by growth and returns, but little margin of safety remains.
AJB.L.rationale: AJ Bell plc (AJB.L), UK investment platform (ii/Dodl rivals); peers are Hargreaves Lansdown (taken private), interactive investor, Charles Schwab, IBKR, LPL, plus UK platforms Quilter.

AX.relative_comps: Axos Financial is a high-growth digital/branchless US bank (rev +14%, 3y CAGR +20%, eps +14%, net margin 22%). The model MoS spread is mixed (Graham 0.80, iv15 0.58 vs EPV -0.14, DCF -0.02) and p_fcf 18 is not meaningful for a bank. ROIC 11% is high for a bank; shares are mid-range (53%) and below sma200. Vs regional banks it is in line to modestly rich on earnings, with the premium justified by growth and efficiency.
AX.rationale: Axos Financial Inc (AX), a US online bank and brokerage-clearing holdco; peers are digital/commercial-lending banks East West, Western Alliance, Customers Bancorp, Merchants, Live Oak.

BION.SW.relative_comps: BB Biotech is a listed closed-end biotech investment company, so company-style multiples (p_fcf 9.6, net margin 752%, eps +664%) are artifacts of mark-to-market gains on the portfolio. The correct valuation yardstick is discount/premium to NAV and the biotech index; the model MoS spread is incoherent (EPV -0.66, Graham -1.0, iv15 0.72). Price is 81% of its 52-wk range and above sma200, i.e. recovering with the biotech tape. It is not comparable to operating financial names on any model metric.
BION.SW.rationale: BB Biotech AG (BION.SW), a Swiss-listed biotech investment trust holding Ionis, Argenx, Insmed etc; true comps are biotech investment trusts/ETFs (XBI, IBB) and Biotech Growth Trust, judged on NAV discount.

CFT.SW.relative_comps: Compagnie Financiere Tradition is a Swiss-listed interdealer broker (Viel group) with modest growth (rev +6%, eps +16%), net margin 12%, ROIC 15% and p_fcf 16.6. It trades near the bottom of its 52-wk range (18% position), below sma200. Model spread is mixed (Graham 0.32 vs EPV -0.62). Versus TP ICAP, BGC and Intercapital it looks in line to modestly cheap, justified by low growth and high cyclicality.
CFT.SW.rationale: Compagnie Financiere Tradition SA (CFT.SW), a voice/hybrid interdealer broker; peers are TP ICAP, BGC Partners, Marex, MarketAxess, Virtu.

IGG.L.relative_comps: IG Group is a UK retail CFD/spread-betting and active-trading platform with an exceptionally high net margin (43%) and ROIC 15%, p_fcf 16.5. The revenue (-38%) and eps (-20%) drops look partly data/disposal driven, so growth is not a clean read. DCF MoS is high (0.50) and EPV 0.21 while Graham/iv15 are negative. Trading at only 5% of its 52-wk range, far below sma200, the market is pricing in regulatory risk (ESMA/FCA leverage rules) and volatility-cycle fade, so the discount is partly justified but looks stretched.
IGG.L.rationale: IG Group Holdings (IGG.L), UK-listed CFD/trading platform (note: ticker is IGG not IG); peers are Plus500, CMC Markets, Saxo, IBKR, Schwab, Futu, Robinhood.

NWG.L.rationale: NatWest Group plc (NWG.L), UK ring-fenced retail/commercial bank; peers are Lloyds, Barclays, HSBC, Standard Chartered, and EU banks BNP, ING, Santander.

Versus specialty insurers and title peers (First American, Fidelity National) it is in line to slightly cheap on P/E and P/B, justified by lower growth than W.R. Berkley-class names.

Against BB Seguridade and Caixa Seguridade it trades at a discount justified by lower margins and more cyclical auto mix, so the valuation is in line.

SEZL.relative_comps: Sezzle is a US/Canada BNPL provider with very high growth (rev +66%, eps +70%, 3y CAGR +53%), net margin 30% but ROIC only 1.7% on this definition. Price sits at 72% of its 52-wk range, well above its 200-day. SEZL.rationale: Sezzle Inc (SEZL), US-listed buy-now-pay-later fintech; peers are Affirm, Klarna, Upstart, SoFi, Enova, OppFi and Zip.

The model MoS spread is positive and high on Graham 0.90, owner earnings 0.73 and EPV 0.31 (DCF/iv15 invalid for a lender). Price sits at only 5% of its 52-wk range, far below sma200, so the market is discounting something (credit costs, policy risk on student lending) beyond what multiples suggest. Versus Synchrony, Ally and Navient it screens cheap with a moderate quality case, a probable partial mispricing.
SLM.rationale: SLM Corp (SLM), US private student-loan originator; peers are Navient, Nelnet, Synchrony, Ally, Capital One, Discover, American Express.

VEFAB.ST.relative_comps: VEF AB (formerly Vostok Emerging Finance) is a Swedish-listed fintech investment company holding stakes in Brazilian/Pakistani/Indian emerging-market fintechs (Creditas, Tinkoff exit, Jazz Cash). Company multiples (net margin 21,687%, p_fcf 6.8) are artifacts of investment gains; the right yardstick is discount to NAV vs Nordic investment companies (Kinnevik, Lundbergs, Latour). A deep NAV discount is typical of the sector and is partly justified by illiquid, hard-to-value fintech marks.
VEFAB.ST.rationale: VEF AB (VEFAB.ST), a Stockholm-listed emerging-markets fintech investment company; peers are Nordic listed investment holdcos such as Kinnevik, Investor, Lundbergs, Latour and Bure.

2607.HK.relative_comps: Shanghai Pharmaceuticals (H-share) is a pharma distributor/manufacturer; at p_fcf ~9x, 10.7% gross margin, 2% net margin and ~5% ROIC it sits at the same low multiple band as Sinopharm and China Resources Pharma, while US wholesalers (Cencora, McKesson, Cardinal) earn higher ROIC and trade richer. EPV/owner-earnings MoS (~44%) and the price near the bottom of its 52-wk range point to a discount, but thin distribution margins, low ROIC and China pricing/VBP pressure explain most of it. Growth is modest (rev +3%, EPS +25% off a low base). Mostly a justified discount, only mildly cheap.
2607.HK.rationale: Shanghai Pharmaceuticals Holdings (2607.HK, medical distribution + pharma manufacturing); peers are the Chinese pharma distribution majors plus the US big-three wholesalers as a global margin benchmark.

ALNY.relative_comps: Alnylam is the RNAi leader (Amvuttra/ATTR-CM) with +65% revenue growth, 82% gross margin and an 8% net margin just turning profitable; ROIC is still negative. At ~48x FCF it is rich on cash-flow multiples versus Ionis/Arrowhead/BioMarin, but those peers are less profitable or slower-growing; the scan prices it near the bottom of its 52-wk range and below its 200-day, so the stock has de-rated sharply. Graham MoS is high while DCF/EPV are not scoreable, so the mispricing case rests on growth durability, not on trailing earnings. Cheap on growth-adjusted terms after the drawdown, rich on trailing FCF.
ALNY.rationale: Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, RNAi therapeutics commercial-stage; true peers are other oligonucleotide/RNA platform and rare-disease commercial biotechs (Ionis, Arrowhead) and high-growth rare-disease franchises (argenx, BioMarin, Sarepta).

BCRX.relative_comps: BioCryst (Orladeyo, oral HAE prophylaxis) shows +94% revenue growth, 98% gross margin and a 30% net margin, at only ~5x p_fcf, with MoS positive on Graham (32%) and iv15 (26%). Versus HAE competitors (KalVista and Pharvaris are pre/early-revenue; Takeda, CSL are large diversified) and profitable rare-disease names like Catalyst and ADMA, it trades at a deep discount, but the Altman Z is -3.1 (heavy debt from Pharmakon royalty financing) and the net margin likely includes one-offs. Price is in the lower third of its range and below sma200. Part of the gap is leverage and Orladeyo competition risk, but the multiple looks well below profitable rare-disease peers.
BCRX.rationale: BioCryst Pharmaceuticals, oral HAE prophylaxis commercial biotech; peers are HAE competitors and profitable small/mid-cap rare-disease specialty pharma.

BONEX.ST.relative_comps: BONESUPPORT (CERAMENT injectable bone-graft substitutes) grows revenue +31% with ~93% gross margin and 12% net margin, but at ~99x p_fcf and a price near the top of its 52-wk range (89%) it is the richest name in the ortho-biologics set; Orthofix, Bioventus, Anika and Integra trade at low-to-mid-teens FCF multiples with lower growth and weaker margins. Altman Z of 74 shows an unlevered balance sheet; ROIC is still slightly negative as it scales (US launch of CERAMENT G). The premium is partly earned by growth and gross margin, but the valuation already discounts a lot of execution.
BONEX.ST.rationale: BONESUPPORT Holding AB (Stockholm), CERAMENT bone-void fillers; peers are orthobiologics and bone-graft/ortho-device companies.

CORT.relative_comps: Corcept (Korlym, relacorilant) has a 98% gross margin, 13% net margin, 18% ROIC and +13% revenue growth, but EPS is down 33% and the FCF multiple is ~62x, far above Catalyst, Harmony, Supernus and Jazz (mid-single to low-teens FCF). Price is mid-range and below sma200 after a sharp fall from the 126 high, and iv15 MoS is -49%, so the model sees it as over-valued relative to its earnings. Growth and quality are decent but not enough to justify a 3-5x multiple premium to profitable specialty-pharma peers unless relacorilant (ovarian cancer) delivers.
CORT.rationale: Corcept Therapeutics, cortisol-modulation specialty pharma (Korlym); peers are profitable single/few-asset specialty and rare-disease pharma companies.

DRW3.DE.relative_comps: Draegerwerk (preferred shares) is a medical + safety technology maker with ~4-5% net margin, 43% gross margin and ~5% ROIC; at ~12.6x p_fcf it is cheaper than Getinge, Philips and Siemens Healthineers, but those have higher margins and returns. Growth is low (rev +3%, EPS +13%), the price sits in the upper range (77%) near its sma200, DCF/EPV MoS are about -26%/-1%, so the discount is largely explained by weak margins and cyclicality. Preferred shares also trade at a structural discount to the voting common. In-line with a justified low multiple.
DRW3.DE.rationale: Draegerwerk AG (DRW3.DE, non-voting preferred shares), anaesthesia/ventilation/patient monitoring plus gas detection and safety; peers are hospital-equipment and critical-care device makers and industrial safety groups.

GMAB.CO.relative_comps: Genmab is a profitable antibody-royalty-plus-product biotech (Darzalex royalties, Epkinly, Tivdak) with 92% gross margin, 26% net margin and 13% ROIC, at ~27x p_fcf, rich-ish versus Incyte/Exelixis but below argenx. The -82% revenue and -87% EPS figures are distorted by a large one-off milestone/comparison base, so growth is not trustworthy; DCF and owner-earnings MoS (~59%/54%) suggest a discount to intrinsic value while EPV is flat. Price is in the upper range (80%) though below its sma200. The gap is a modest discount if Darzalex royalties plus the Merus acquisition product pipeline hold.
GMAB.CO.rationale: Genmab A/S (Copenhagen), antibody and bispecific oncology biotech with royalty income; peers are profitable mid-cap antibody/oncology biotechs.

GNS.L.relative_comps: Genus plc is a porcine and bovine genetics company (PIC, ABS), not a classic drug biotech; its industry tag is misleading. Price is in the lower quarter of its range and below sma200; Graham MoS (76%) is flattering and owner-earnings MoS only 7%. Real quality is that of a niche genetics business with PRRS-resistant pig regulatory optionality, not of a high-ROIC animal-health leader like Zoetis.
GNS.L.rationale: Genus plc (LSE), animal genetics (PIC pigs, ABS cattle); peers are animal-health and livestock-genetics/inputs businesses, not human biotech. Reported margins look distorted.

GUBRA.CO.rationale: Gubra A/S (Copenhagen), obesity-focused preclinical CRO and peptide drug discovery; peers are discovery CROs and Danish/European obesity peptide names.

HRMY.relative_comps: Harmony (Wakix for narcolepsy) trades at ~5.7x p_fcf with 77% gross margin, 18% net margin, 19% ROIC and +22% revenue growth; DCF MoS is 59%, owner earnings 31%. Price is mid-range and below sma200.
HRMY.rationale: Harmony Biosciences, sleep/neurology specialty pharma (Wakix); peers are CNS/sleep and rare-disease specialty pharma companies.

INVA.rationale: Innoviva, Inc., royalty-driven specialty biopharma; peers are royalty aggregators (Royalty Pharma, Ligand, XOMA) and small specialty pharma.

MOH.rationale: Molina Healthcare, government-sponsored managed care (Medicaid, Medicare, Marketplace); peers are Centene, Elevance, UnitedHealth, Humana and smaller managed-care plans.

UHS.rationale: Universal Health Services, US acute-care and behavioral health hospital operator; peers are for-profit hospital operators (HCA, Tenet, CHS) and behavioral-health providers (Acadia).

Against Viking, Structure and Altimmune, Zealand is more de-risked via big-pharma partnerships and cash, so it screens cheap even after normalising for milestones.
ZEAL.CO.rationale: Zealand Pharma A/S (Copenhagen), peptide/obesity and metabolic therapeutics with big-pharma partnerships; peers are obesity-focused biotechs and the incumbents Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly.

The gap is largely justified: ROIC is ~4.6%, net margin ~0.4%, EPS fell ~56%, revenue is flat and Altman Z ~1.8 with a heavy lease load, while Ahold and Tesco earn clearly higher returns and Carrefour is exiting or restructuring weak markets (Italy, Poland, Brazil exposure). The cheap multiple is a classic cyclical trap, not a clean mispricing; ROIC ~23% and net margin ~11% are still well above Pilgrim's, Tyson or Hormel, but they are mean-reverting. Versus Vital Farms (premium pasture-raised, growth, richer multiple) it is cheap, versus commodity protein peers roughly in line on normalised earnings. Net: justified discount, so in line.
CALM.rationale: Cal-Maine Foods is a US commodity shell-egg producer with some prepared foods; closest comps are Vital Farms (eggs) and the commodity animal-protein group (Pilgrim's, Tyson, Seaboard, Post's egg business).

The MoS spread is mixed (DCF/Graham positive, EPV deeply negative). The multiple reflects a sticky dividend and a net-cash-like balance sheet more than growth, so it is rich against peers.

Revenue is flat (-0.7%), EPS -17%, ROIC ~14% and net margin ~6% (post-excise reporting), so the gap to PMI is justified by the lack of a scaled smoke-free engine, while the gap to BAT is small. Cash returns are strong and price sits mid-range, so it is a defensive value read, not a mispricing.
IMB.L.rationale: Imperial Brands plc (IMB.L) is a UK-listed combustible-heavy tobacco group (Davidoff, Gauloises, blu); peers are the global tobacco majors (BAT, Philip Morris, Altria, Japan Tobacco) and Scandinavian Tobacco Group.

LRN.relative_comps: Stride (online K-12 curriculum and career learning) trades at p_fcf ~10x with a positive DCF/owner-earnings/Graham spread (EPV ~0), against Grand Canyon and Adtalem at mid-teens FCF multiples and Strategic Education/Perdoceo roughly 10-13x. Growth is modest (revenue +5%, 3y CAGR ~11%, EPS +20%) with net margin ~13% and ROIC ~11%, which is lower than Grand Canyon but comparable to Adtalem and Strategic. Price is down from its 52-week high and under its 200-day average after a platform and enrolment execution scare. Mildly cheap versus the higher-quality US for-profit education names, with the discount partly deserved by regulatory and funding-per-pupil dependence.
LRN.rationale: Stride Inc (LRN) runs publicly funded virtual K-12 schools plus career learning; peers are US for-profit and online education operators (Grand Canyon, Adtalem, Strategic Education, Perdoceo, APEI) and K-12 learning platforms.

NWL.MI.relative_comps: Newlat Food (Italian dairy, pasta, bakery and private-label packaged food, owner of the Princes preserved-food business) shows p_fcf ~2.6x and a large positive MoS across DCF, owner-earnings, EPV and iv15, but revenue +80% and EPS +142% are acquisition/scope effects (Princes), not organic growth, so the trailing numbers are not comparable to peers. ROIC ~6.6%, Altman Z ~1.7 and a leveraged balance sheet argue the very low FCF multiple reflects debt and integration risk rather than a free lunch. Versus Orsero, Valsoia or Bonduelle it screens cheap, but data quality is poor and I would not call it a clean mispricing. Treat as cheap with low confidence.
NWL.MI.rationale: Newlat Food SpA (NWL.MI) is a Milan-listed Italian packaged-food group; Italian and European mid-cap food manufacturers are the real peers, with Princes as the closest direct comp for the UK-consolidated business; medium confidence on the scope of consolidation.

PPC.relative_comps: Pilgrim's Pride (US/Mexico/Europe chicken) trades at p_fcf ~10x with a positive DCF/Graham/owner-earnings spread (EPV negative), in line with Tyson and JBS and cheaper than Hormel on absolute multiples. Gross margin ~13% and net margin ~6% are the usual commodity-chicken profile, revenue +3.5%, EPS flat and ROIC ~10%, and chicken margins are near the cycle's best, so the headline cheapness leans on peak-ish earnings. Price sits close to the bottom of its 52-week range, a bit weak versus peers, but not a standalone mispricing.
PPC.rationale: Pilgrim's Pride is a JBS-controlled pure-play chicken producer; peers are Tyson, JBS, BRF/MBRF, Hormel (Jennie-O), Seaboard and other commodity animal-protein producers.

SFD.relative_comps: Smithfield Foods (US pork leader, packaged meats, post-2025 IPO, majority owned by WH Group) trades at p_fcf ~10.5x with a mixed spread (DCF/Graham/owner-earnings positive, EPV -34%), roughly in line with Tyson and Hormel and richer than parent WH Group (single-digit earnings multiple). Revenue +9.8%, ROIC ~5% and net margin ~6% are sound but not exceptional; packaged-meats mix gives a steadier margin than pure commodity peers, offset by hog-cycle exposure. Price is near the bottom of its 52-week range, a sign of recent weakness. Fair, not a mispricing.
SFD.rationale: Smithfield Foods (SFD) is a US pork processor and packaged-meat brand owner controlled by WH Group; peers are Hormel, Tyson, JBS, Pilgrim's and WH Group in Hong Kong.

SFM.relative_comps: Sprouts Farmers Market (natural and organic specialty grocer) trades at p_fcf ~11x versus Kroger and Albertsons roughly 10-15x and Natural Grocers lower-teens, but it grows faster (revenue +14%, EPS +42%) with a gross margin ~37% versus ~22-28% for conventional grocers and ROIC ~11%. DCF and EPV MoS are negative (-7%, -72%), so the model view is that the rebound already prices a good deal of its growth, even though Graham and owner-earnings are positive. Price sits close to the bottom of its recent range after a sharp fall on slowing comps, so growth-adjusted it screens cheap versus conventional grocers, but valuation methods disagree.
SFM.rationale: Sprouts Farmers Market is a US specialty grocer focused on fresh, natural and organic; real comps are US grocers (Kroger, Albertsons, Natural Grocers, Weis, Ingles) and big-box rivals Costco, Walmart and BJ's.

TPB.relative_comps: Turning Point Brands (Zig-Zag papers, Stoker's, Fre and Altair nicotine pouches) trades at the richest p_fcf in the group (~24x) with a negative EPV, DCF and owner-earnings MoS, versus Altria, BAT and Imperial at ~8-11x and Philip Morris at ~20x. Growth justifies a premium over combustible peers: revenue +28%, EPS +45%, gross margin ~57%, ROIC ~12%, driven by pouch ramp-up, but this is a small-cap with Zig-Zag concentration and no scale against Zyn, Velo and on!. Price is near its 52-week high, so the growth is already priced; rich versus peers rather than cheap.
TPB.rationale: Turning Point Brands (TPB) is a US small-cap with rolling-paper, smokeless/chewing-tobacco and nicotine-pouch exposure; peers are Altria, Philip Morris, BAT and Imperial for the pouch race, and Universal Corp and Scandinavian Tobacco for smaller tobacco names.

0914.HK.relative_comps: Anhui Conch is the lowest-cost, strongest-balance-sheet Chinese cement major; p_fcf ~10.9 and net margin ~10% sit above domestic peers (BBMG, CR Building Materials, Huaxin) whose margins are thinner and leverage higher, and roughly in line with Western majors on cash multiple though with far lower growth. Revenue is shrinking (-12% yoy, -15% 3y CAGR) on the China property slump, but eps is flat-to-up on cost discipline. Price sits ~13% off its 52-wk position range and below the 200d SMA, so trend is weak; the discount to Holcim/Heidelberg is mostly justified by China property deflation and cement overcapacity, with a modest quality premium to Chinese peers deserved. Mixed MoS spread (DCF/Graham positive, owner earnings negative) argues in-line, not a clear mispricing.
0914.HK.rationale: Anhui Conch Cement, China's largest cement producer by capacity; true peers are Chinese cement and building-materials majors plus global heavy-materials groups.

1208.HK.relative_comps: MMG (Las Bambas, Kinsevere, Khoemacau, Dugald River) trades at p_fcf ~7.4 versus ~15-30x for FCX/SCCO/ANTO, and with MoS positive on EPV and DCF it screens cheap. Growth is strong (rev +39%, eps +179% on the copper price spike and Khoemacau), but margins (net ~8%, roic ~9.5%) are well below SCCO/FCX quality, and the stock is near its 52-wk high (proximity ~5%, well above SMA200), so much of the re-rating has happened. Discount is partly justified by Peru community/blockade risk at Las Bambas, China Minmetals control, high leverage and Hong Kong listing discount; remaining gap is a modest real mispricing but with elevated geopolitical risk.
1208.HK.rationale: MMG Limited, Minmetals-controlled copper/zinc miner listed in Hong Kong; peers are listed copper pure plays and diversified miners.

1378.HK.relative_comps: China Hongqiao is the largest integrated Chinese aluminium producer (own power, alumina and Indonesian bauxite/alumina). p_fcf ~5.6 and net margin ~14% (best in the group) versus Alcoa/Century at low-teens multiples and thin margins; Graham/DCF/owner-earnings MoS are all strongly positive. Growth is modest (rev +4%, eps flat) and price is close to its 52-wk range top (proximity ~7%) well above SMA200, so momentum is strong. The discount to Western aluminum names is only partly justified by Chinese capacity-cap policy, Xinjiang/forced-labour supply-chain concerns, dividend-driven holder base and HK listing; on margins and cost position it still looks cheap.
1378.HK.rationale: China Hongqiao Group, vertically integrated aluminium smelter/alumina producer; peers are global and Chinese primary aluminium producers.

2600.HK.relative_comps: Aluminum Corp of China (Chalco) is the state-owned alumina/aluminium major with bauxite, alumina, primary aluminium and some energy. p_fcf ~4.9 and mid-to-high EPV/DCF/owner-earnings MoS (51%/68%/47%) make it the cheapest of the Chinese group, but gross margin 17% and net margin 5% trail Hongqiao (25%/14%) and revenue is flat. Price is at its 52-wk high (proximity ~1%) well above SMA200 on the aluminium price run. Discount to Hongqiao is largely justified by lower margins, SOE capital allocation, heavy alumina exposure and trade-flow with lower integration; still cheap versus Alcoa/Hydro on cash multiple.
2600.HK.rationale: Aluminum Corporation of China Ltd (Chinalco H-share), integrated alumina/aluminium producer; peers are Chinese and global aluminium producers.

CTVA.relative_comps: Corteva (seed + crop protection, post-DuPont/Dow spin) is the global #2 in seeds and #4-5 in crop protection. p_fcf ~2.3 looks anomalously low (likely a data artefact from working-capital seasonality), while MoS on EPV, DCF and owner earnings is 67-76%; against FMC (distressed, falling margins) and Bayer (litigation overhang) Corteva has far better quality: gross margin 47%, steady revenue, eps +23%. Low roic (~4.9%) reflects large goodwill and altman_z ~0.95 is a flagged data/model quirk for an investment-grade balance sheet. Price is near 52-wk lows area (proximity ~7%) and below SMA200, so trend is weak. Discount to Nutrien/Mosaic is not justified given seed-trait moat; looks cheap but the FCF data should be verified.
CTVA.rationale: Corteva Inc, US ag seed and crop-protection company; peers are crop-protection and seed majors plus ag-input names.

KWS.DE.relative_comps: KWS Saat is a Germany-based plant-breeding specialist (sugar beet, corn, cereals, vegetables) with a 61% gross margin but only ~10% net margin due to heavy R&D. p_fcf ~26 and DCF MoS of -100% mark it rich against Corteva and Vilmorin on cash multiples, with EPV MoS slightly negative; revenue is flat (-3% yoy) and roic ~7%. Price is ~17% from the top of its 52-wk range and near SMA200, so trend is neutral. A premium for family-controlled sugar-beet leadership and pure-breeding franchise is partly justified, but growth does not support a 26x FCF multiple versus Corteva.
KWS.DE.rationale: KWS SAAT SE & Co. KGaA (Einbeck, Germany), plant breeder; peers are seed/trait companies, not crop-protection chemicals.

SLVM.relative_comps: Sylvamo is the global leader in uncoated freesheet paper (Latin America, Europe, North America) after spin from International Paper. p_fcf ~36 and eps -55% yoy with revenue -11% show a cyclical earnings trough; roic ~13.7% is high for the group though, and gross margin 22% sits in line with Mondi/Navigator. MoS spread is positive on DCF (43%), Graham (70%) and owner earnings (51%) but EPV only 8%. Price is ~31% off the 52-wk range top and below SMA200, a downtrend. Premium multiple on trough FCF is justified by roic and declining-but-consolidating paper market; relative to peers it is rich on trailing FCF but cheap on normalised earnings, so net in line.
SLVM.rationale: Sylvamo Corp, uncoated freesheet paper producer; peers are paper/pulp and packaging producers.

SOLB.BR.relative_comps: Syensqo (specialty materials spun out of Solvay: Materials, Composites, Oil & Gas/Consumer & Industrial) trades on p_fcf ~6.5 with DCF/Graham/owner-earnings MoS of 60-72% against Evonik/Arkema/Lanxess which trade at ~8-15x FCF. But net margin ~0.6%, eps -87%, revenue -7% and 3y revenue CAGR -33% show a deep earnings trough plus Solvay perimeter effects; altman_z ~1.3 and high debt after aerospace/battery material exposure. Price is ~33% from the top of the 52-wk range and below SMA200. The discount is largely justified by earnings collapse and balance-sheet leverage, though the valuation gap on normalised cash flow suggests a modest mispricing if aerospace composites recover.
SOLB.BR.rationale: Syensqo SA (Brussels listing SOLB.BR is the Solvay spin-off specialty chemicals company); verified from universe sector/industry as Chemicals; peers are European specialty-chemical names.

SSRM.relative_comps: SSR Mining (Cripple Creek & Victor, Seabee, Puna, Cripple/Çöpler ex-Turkey) is a mid-tier gold producer. p_fcf ~24 is rich versus Kinross/Agnico/Equinox (~10-20x), with DCF, EPV and owner-earnings MoS all at -100% but Graham +79%. Revenue is +67% yoy (Çöpler restart partial base effect) and net margin 24% is strong, but roic ~2.2% is the weakest in the group. Price sits ~37% off 52-wk range top and above SMA200, a recovering trend. Premium multiple is not justified by quality: roic is poor and Çöpler remains operationally uncertain, so SSRM screens rich versus peers unless gold stays elevated.
SSRM.rationale: SSR Mining Inc (Nasdaq/TSX: SSRM), mid-tier gold producer; peers are mid-cap gold miners.

STP.WA.relative_comps: Stalprodukt (Bochnia, Poland) makes cold-formed steel sections, wheel rims (Fuchs) and stainless steel components; identity inferred from .WA venue and PLN price (~230) plus the Steel industry tag, so identification is moderately confident. Gross margin ~6%, net margin -1.4%, revenue -2% (3y CAGR -14%) mark a weak earnings profile; p_fcf shows 0.0 (missing data, not genuinely zero) so cash-multiple comparison is not possible. DCF MoS +61% but EPV -25% and owner earnings -100%, a mixed set. Price is mid-range (proximity ~48%) and below SMA200. Versus Polish and EU steel processors it is in line: low-margin metal-forming with no clear mispricing and no valid FCF multiple.
STP.WA.rationale: Stalprodukt S.A. (Warsaw-listed Polish steel product maker); peers are European steel processors and Polish metal groups. Moderate identity confidence; FCF data missing.

A2A.MI.relative_comps: A2A SpA (Milan multi-utility: generation, networks, waste-to-energy, retail) screens cheap on p_fcf (~7.6x) against Hera, Iren, Enel and Engie, which sit at roughly 10-15x. The Graham-revised MoS is high but DCF and EPV are -1.0 (model non-convergence on a levered, capex-heavy utility), so the multi-method spread is mostly one method. Growth is mixed (revenue +9% yoy but a negative 3y CAGR and EPS -14%), margins are thin and ROIC (~5%) is in line with Italian multi-utility peers. Altman Z ~1.1 is typical for a levered utility. Price is mid-range (52-wk proximity ~0.35, below the 200-day average). Verdict: modestly cheap, but the p_fcf gap is largely explained by lumpy FCF and the capex cycle, so it is not a clean mispricing.
A2A.MI.rationale: Verified from universe data as a Milan-listed Diversified Utilities name. A2A is the Lombardy multi-utility with generation, regulated distribution, waste-to-energy and retail. True peers are the other Italian multi-utilities (Hera, Iren, ACEA) plus ERG, EDP and Enel for generation and networks.

CGAS3.SA.relative_comps: CGAS3 (Companhia de Gas de Sao Paulo, Comgas) is a regulated gas distribution concession in Brazil, a Cosan subsidiary. p_fcf ~5.4x and a DCF MoS ~0.71 look cheap against global gas distributors (Atmos, NJR, Snam, ~15-25x), but those peers trade at developed-market multiples with lower rates. Revenue is -25% yoy and EPS -14%, so growth is deteriorating, while gross margin ~30%, net margin ~13% and ROIC ~19% are strong for a regulated name. The price is at the 52-wk low (proximity 0.0, below the 200-day average), which is negative momentum. EPV is -0.56 and owner-earnings MoS is ~0, so the DCF-only signal is not corroborated. The discount is partly a Brazil rate and country-risk premium plus a thin free float and controlling-holder dynamics. Verdict: cheap on headline metrics, but a good part of the gap is justified. Check tariff-review risk.
CGAS3.SA.rationale: The .SA suffix is B3 Sao Paulo. CGAS3 is the common share of Companhia de Gas de Sao Paulo (Comgas), which is controlled by Cosan. Peers are Brazilian regulated utilities (Sabesp, Copel, Energisa), parent Cosan, and international gas distributors for the business model.

CNA.L.relative_comps: Centrica (British Gas, Centrica Business Solutions, Bord Gais, upstream gas, nuclear stake) trades at ~24x p_fcf on a depressed FCF base. That is rich against SSE and Engie, but the EPV (+0.79) and owner-earnings (+0.76) MoS spreads are high, which signals earnings power well above the current price on normalised retail and trading margins. Revenue and EPS are flat to down, and net margin is ~0 on the latest year, but ROIC (~39%) is very high on a small capital base. Price is below the 200-day average and in the lower half of its 52-wk range (proximity ~0.22). Centrica is an energy retailer and trader, not a regulated utility, so multiples against regulated networks mislead. Verdict: in-line to cheap on earnings power with a wide model spread. The p_fcf view is rich because cash flow is lumpy through working capital and trading collateral.
CNA.L.rationale: Verified from universe data as an Independent Power Producers name on the LSE. CNA.L is Centrica plc. True peers are the UK integrated energy retailers and generators (SSE, Drax) and EU integrated utilities (Engie, EDF), not regulated network operators.

ELEC.PA.relative_comps: Electricite de Strasbourg (ES Energies Strasbourg, about 88% owned by EDF, small float) is an Alsace electricity distribution and heat network operator with a thin free float. p_fcf ~7.6x, a Graham MoS of ~0.80 and DCF/EPV MoS of 0.25 and 0.14 look cheap against regulated networks (Elia, Redeia, Terna at ~12-20x). But low ROIC (~6%), revenue -12% yoy and a thin gross margin (~16%) are typical of a pass-through distributor. The price is near a 52-wk low zone (proximity ~0.18, below the 200-day average). The discount reflects minority-holder illiquidity, the parent's control and capped regulated returns, not an obvious mispricing. Verdict: cheap on screens, partly justified by structure.
ELEC.PA.rationale: ELEC.PA is Electricite de Strasbourg (ES Energies Strasbourg), a regulated Alsace distributor and heat supplier controlled by EDF. Confirmed from the Regulated Electric classification in the universe data. Closest comps are other regulated electricity distributors and transmission operators, plus EDF and Engie as parent-group references.

KGN.WA.relative_comps: Kogeneracja SA (Wroclaw, Poland, CHP heat and power, majority owned by EPH) is the cheapest name in the set on p_fcf (~2.7x) with DCF MoS ~0.72, Graham ~0.87 and IV15 ~0.79. EPV is -1.0 and owner-earnings -0.18, so the signal is not corroborated by every method. Growth is the best in the group (EPS +37%, 3y revenue CAGR +13.5%), net margin ~10% is solid, but ROIC is only ~6%. The price is near its 52-wk high (proximity ~0.95, above the 200-day average), so the re-rating has already started. Against Polish peers PGE, Enea and Tauron, it is cheaper on FCF multiple, but it carries regulatory risk on CO2 and heat tariffs and has a small cap and low liquidity. Verdict: cheap on the numbers and partly justified by the CHP risk profile and cash-flow lumpiness.
KGN.WA.rationale: KGN.WA is Kogeneracja S.A. on the Warsaw exchange, a CHP operator supplying heat and power to Wroclaw and surrounding areas, with EPH as controlling shareholder. Peers are the Polish utilities (PGE, Tauron, Enea, ZE PAK) and CEE/Nordic CHP operators (Fortum, Verbund).

TPE.WA.relative_comps: Tauron Polska Energia is a Polish vertically integrated utility (coal and renewables generation, mining, distribution, retail). p_fcf ~32x looks rich against PGE and Enea, and DCF, EPV, owner-earnings MoS are all -1.0 with Graham at -0.82, so the multi-method spread shows no margin of safety. EPS +473% yoy comes off a depressed base, which flatters earnings-yield-gap. ROIC (~3%) is the lowest of the group, margins are mid (net ~10%), revenue is -3% yoy and Altman Z is ~1.4. Price is in the lower half of its 52-wk range (proximity ~0.30, below the 200-day average). The discount to Polish peers is not clearly a mispricing: heavy coal exposure, transition capex and state-aid dependence justify weak valuation support. Verdict: rich on cash flow, with no valuation cushion.
TPE.WA.rationale: TPE.WA is Tauron Polska Energia S.A. on the Warsaw exchange, a Silesia-based vertically integrated state-linked utility. Closest comps are PGE, Enea and ZE PAK in Poland, and CEZ and EVN in the wider CEE region.
