DVL.WA.relative_comps: Develia (ex-LC Corp) is a Polish residential developer with a smaller rental book, so its true comps are Dom Development, Atal, Archicom, Ronson, Murapol and Echo, not the broad Real Estate sector. Valuation is mixed: P/FCF about 23x is rich for a developer because project cash flow is lumpy, and DCF/EPV MoS are negative, while Graham (+82%) and owner-earnings (+32%) MoS are positive. That spread reflects book/land-bank value against thin near-term cash, so the cheapness is not clean. Growth is solid (rev +16% yoy, 3y CAGR ~25%, eps +14%) and net margin of 21% with ROIC of ~10% is respectable, though below best-in-class Dom/Atal on returns. Price is near the 52-week low (about 0.21 from the low) and close to the 200-day average, so momentum is weak. The discount to the Polish developer group is partly justified by the cash conversion and lower-quality ROIC; a real mispricing needs the land bank/book value to be confirmed.
DVL.WA.rationale: DVL.WA is Develia S.A. (formerly LC Corp, Wroclaw), a Warsaw-listed residential developer, so its peers are the Polish listed developers Dom Development, Atal, Archicom, Ronson, Murapol and Echo Investment. Identity confirmed from industry tag Real Estate - Development and the .WA suffix. Peer multiples come from sector knowledge, not the universe file.

HEM.ST.relative_comps: Hemnet Group is Sweden's dominant property listing portal (classified as Real Estate - Development by the data vendor, which is a mis-tag; a ~100% gross margin and 34% net margin are those of an online classifieds platform). Its true comps are Rightmove, REA Group, Scout24 (ImmoScout24), Zillow, plus Auto Trader and Carsales as asset-light classifieds. On valuation, P/FCF of ~9.7x and positive DCF/owner-earnings MoS (+30%/+33%) look cheap against peers that typically trade at mid-teens to 25x+ cash flow. Growth (rev +9%, 3y CAGR ~20%, eps +10%) and ROIC of ~19% are decent but decelerating versus its history. The price sits at the 52-week low (proximity 0.0, about 187 high vs roughly 61 low) and well below the 200-day average, so the de-rating is severe. The gap is partly justified by thesis risk (slowing listing volumes, pushback on pricing, competition and disintermediation risk), but a ~65% drawdown with the margin profile intact looks like a possible overshoot, not yet confirmed as a mispricing.
HEM.ST.rationale: HEM.ST is Hemnet Group AB, the Stockholm-listed Swedish property portal. The Real Estate - Development tag is wrong for the economics: gross margin about 100% and net margin 34% identify an asset-light online marketplace. True peers are the listed property and classifieds portals Rightmove, REA, Scout24, Zillow, Auto Trader and Carsales.

IMC.MC.relative_comps: Unmapped. The ticker IMC.MC could not be matched with confidence to a specific Madrid-listed company, and the universe file only gives the Real Estate - Development tag, so no peer set is asserted. The data show ~97% gross margin and 36% net margin (property-rental-like), low P/FCF (~6.4x), positive DCF/owner-earnings MoS but negative EPV, eps -66% yoy and ROIC of ~3.7%. Price is about 0.30 from the 52-week low and near the 200-day average. A valuation gap versus peers cannot be assessed without confirming the company.
IMC.MC.rationale: IMC.MC is not a ticker I recognize with certainty. It could be a small Spanish real-estate company, but guessing the identity from the letters risks a wrong peer set; the issuer name must be verified externally before clustering. Do not carry a peer-multiple read for this name.

RITM.relative_comps: Rithm Capital is a hybrid mortgage REIT / asset manager (Newrez originations and servicing, MSR portfolio, Sculptor, single-family and commercial real estate). Its closest comps are Annaly, AGNC, Starwood Property Trust and Blackstone Mortgage for the REIT book, and PennyMac Financial and Mr. Cooper for the mortgage-servicing and origination side. Standard industrial metrics (P/FCF 0, DCF/EPV -100%, Altman Z about -0.08) are not meaningful for a financial and should be ignored; Graham (+40%) and owner-earnings (+26%) MoS are the only usable signals, and P/book and dividend yield are the real yardsticks. Revenue growth is high (+20%, 3y CAGR ~50% via acquisitions) but eps fell 38% and ROIC is low at 2.4%, so earnings quality lags. Price is below the 200-day average and about 0.17 from the 52-week low. It looks in line with the mortgage-REIT group: the diversified model and dividend deserve a modest premium to pure agency REITs, offset by earnings volatility.
RITM.rationale: RITM is Rithm Capital Corp (NYSE), formerly New Residential. It is a mortgage REIT with large operating subsidiaries, so peers are the mortgage REITs and mortgage servicers listed above, not equity REITs or developers. P/book was not in the universe data, so the peer rank rests on sector knowledge and is low confidence.

BYIT.L.relative_comps: Universe file carries no p_fcf, MoS or growth data for this name (only the ev_gp methodology tag), so the ranking is qualitative. Bytes is a capital-light Microsoft-licensing and security reseller with very high net margin and ROIC for the group and a net-cash balance sheet, which usually earns a premium to low-margin IT distributors like Computacenter, Bechtle and CDW. Growth has been slow and Microsoft partner-incentive changes are a real margin risk. Treat it as in line to modestly rich unless the multi-method MoS shows otherwise. Check price vs sma200 and 52-week position in the scan before calling any gap a mispricing.
BYIT.L.rationale: Bytes Technology Group (LSE: BYIT) is a UK software reseller and services provider built around Microsoft licensing. Closest comps are Softcat, Computacenter, SoftwareOne, Bechtle, Cancom, CDW, Insight and SHI.

DFH.relative_comps: Universe file carries no p_fcf, MoS or growth data for this name (methodology tags rd_capitalized_dcf, owner_earnings, epv), so the ranking is qualitative. Dream Finders is an asset-light, high-growth Southeast and Mid-Atlantic homebuilder that grows through acquisitions and uses a lot of lot-option and leverage. It typically trades at a lower P/E and book multiple than DHI, PHM and NVR, which reflects its thinner gross margin, higher leverage and weaker cash conversion while it grows. The discount is partly justified by that quality gap, but its growth is above the peer median. Read it as cheap vs peers on earnings, with the open question being cyclicality and rate exposure shared by the whole group. Free cash flow is lumpy in homebuilders, so p_fcf is a poor valuation yardstick here; use P/E and P/B.
DFH.rationale: Dream Finders Homes (NYSE: DFH) is a Jacksonville-based US homebuilder (also with a mortgage and title arm). Peers are listed US homebuilders, led by the large caps DHI, LEN, PHM and the mid-caps TMHC, MTH, MHO, CCS and LGIH.

TKA.DE.relative_comps: Priced on p_fcf 62x with negative ROIC, -6% revenue and ~1% net margin, it is not cheap on cash flow; the discount to peers is mostly an asset-value (steel, marine systems, materials services) story, and EPV/Graham/owner-earnings all read -100% MoS. Versus Salzgitter, voestalpine, ArcelorMittal and Outokumpu it has weaker margins and shrinking sales but a similar cyclical trough profile. Price sits ~0.57 of the 52-wk range near the 200d average, so there is no momentum edge. The gap to peers looks justified by quality, not a mispricing.
TKA.DE.rationale: thyssenkrupp AG (Essen): steel, materials services, automotive tech, marine systems. Peers are European integrated and specialty steel producers plus steel distributors, which drive its earnings; the conglomerate label hides a steel-cycle business.

TOR.WA.relative_comps: Torpol screens very cheap on p_fcf (2.8x) with positive DCF/EPV/owner-earnings MoS and a 17% ROIC, against Polish rail/road builders like Budimex and Unibep that trade at mid-teens FCF multiples. Growth is strong (revenue +36% yoy, 22% 3y CAGR) though gross margin is thin at 7%, typical of contractors. Price is only ~0.17 off the 52-wk low and below the 200d average, so momentum is weak and the market is discounting backlog or working-capital risk. Mostly a real mispricing, with order-book lumpiness and a single-client (PKP PLK) dependence as the caveat.
TOR.WA.rationale: Torpol S.A. (Poznan): Polish railway and rail-infrastructure contractor, exposed to PKP PLK/EU-funded rail capex. True peers are Polish and Central European civil and rail contractors.

VEI.OL.relative_comps: Veidekke trades at ~11x p_fcf with positive DCF/Graham/owner-earnings MoS but EPV MoS of -53%, so on a steady-state view it is fully priced. Its 20% ROIC and net-cash balance (Altman 3.1) beat Skanska, NCC and Peab, with eps +24%. Revenue growth is modest (+4%) and the 1.0 gross margin is a data artifact for a contractor. Price is ~0.95 of the 52-wk range and above the 200d average, so momentum is strong. The premium to Nordic builders is justified by returns and a clean balance sheet, so it is in line to slightly rich.
VEI.OL.rationale: Veidekke ASA (Oslo): Norwegian and Nordic construction and property development. Peers are Nordic and European listed builders (Skanska, NCC, Peab, Implenia, Strabag).

VOLO.ST.relative_comps: On the reported numbers (p_fcf 3x, DCF MoS +74%, EPV MoS +56%) it looks deeply cheap versus Lifco, Indutrade and Lagercrantz, which trade at 25x+ FCF. But the data are internally inconsistent: a year range of 22-116 with price pinned ~2% from the low, a 7% gross margin and 4% net margin do not match a Swedish serial-acquirer profile. Treat the multiples as unreliable until the price series and share count (possible split or unit error) are verified. If the figures are real, the fall of roughly 80% from the high would be a distress signal rather than cheapness.
VOLO.ST.rationale: Volati AB (Stockholm): Swedish industrial and trading conglomerate and serial acquirer. Peers are Nordic acquisitive industrial holding groups. Identity matches the ticker, but the scan figures look corrupted, so the verdict is held at in_line instead of calling a bargain.

WBD.MI.relative_comps: Webuild has no usable p_fcf (0.0 means missing), and its Altman Z of 0.84 flags balance-sheet stress against ACS, Vinci, Ferrovial and Hochtief. Revenue is growing +15% yoy (18% 3y CAGR) and eps +20%, which beats most European majors, but net margin is 2% and ROIC 3.5%. DCF, Graham and IV15 MoS are strongly positive while EPV and owner earnings are negative, so the apparent discount depends on assuming backlog converts to cash. Price is near the lower part of its 52-wk range (~0.22) and under the 200d average. Cheap on assets and backlog, but the discount is partly earned by leverage and low returns.
WBD.MI.rationale: Webuild S.p.A. (Milan): Italy's largest international civil and infrastructure contractor (dams, rail, metro, bridges) with a large state-backed backlog. Peers are the European infrastructure and construction majors.

WWI.OL.relative_comps: Wilh. Wilhelmsen Holding is a holding company, so the 53% net margin reflects equity-accounted income from Wallenius Wilhelmsen and other stakes, not operating margin. P_fcf of 28x looks rich, yet Graham and owner-earnings MoS are strongly positive (+91% / +56%) while DCF and EPV show -100% (not meaningful for a holding). Growth is solid (revenue +9%, eps +35%), ROIC is low at 5%, and price is high in its 52-wk range (~0.86) and above the 200d average. Versus Wallenius Wilhelmsen, Hoegh Autoliners and Hyundai Glovis the holding company probably trades at a discount to NAV but looks in line on cash-flow multiples. Treat the discount as structural, not a clear mispricing.
WWI.OL.rationale: Wilh. Wilhelmsen Holding ASA (Oslo): maritime holding company with stakes in Wallenius Wilhelmsen (car and ro-ro shipping), Hyundai Glovis, NorSea and Treasure. Peers are the shipping operators it owns plus Norwegian industrial holding companies.

000270.KS.relative_comps: Kia (Hyundai Motor group) trades at p_fcf ~7 with a 63-80% multi-method MoS, but the whole global-OEM cohort (Hyundai Motor, Toyota, Honda, GM, Ford, Stellantis) is at single-digit FCF multiples, so the discount is a sector/Korea-discount feature rather than a Kia-specific mispricing. Growth is modest (rev +6%, EPS -22% on US tariff costs) and gross margin ~20% / ROIC ~11% are mid-pack, better than Stellantis/Ford and below Toyota. Price sits ~25% under its 52wk high vs the 200d, so momentum is weak; cheap vs peers but largely justified by tariff and cyclical risk.
000270.KS.rationale: Korean mass-market auto OEM (Kia Corp) closely tied to Hyundai Motor; global volume OEMs are the true comps.

012330.KS.relative_comps: Hyundai Mobis (captive Hyundai/Kia module and parts supplier) shows p_fcf ~11 and mixed MoS (Graham 80%, EPV negative) against tier-1 suppliers like Magna, Lear, Aptiv and Denso on 8-15x FCF. Gross margin ~14% and ROIC ~4% are weak vs Denso/Aptiv but typical of a captive module assembler; EPS -9% reflects tariff and EV-transition cost. Valuation is in line with peers; the captive-customer link to Hyundai/Kia caps the rerating case, so no clear mispricing.
012330.KS.rationale: Korean captive tier-1 auto parts/module maker (Hyundai Mobis); peers are global tier-1 suppliers and the sister company HL Mando.

0175.HK.relative_comps: Geely Automobile (Geely/Zeekr/Lynk brands, Volvo-affiliated) trades at p_fcf ~2.8, the cheap end of Chinese OEMs, with revenue +44% yoy and 3y CAGR 33% versus slower Great Wall and Chery growth. Net margin ~5% and gross ~17% are in line with BYD/Chery; ROIC of 2.5% is low. Price is within 2% of the 52wk high, trend strong. The low FCF multiple partly reflects China price-war and working-capital payables; growth plus momentum argue it is genuinely cheap relative to quality-adjusted peers, but cash conversion should be verified.
0175.HK.rationale: Hong Kong-listed Zhejiang Geely Automobile Holdings, Chinese mass-market and NEV OEM.

1880.HK.relative_comps: China Tourism Group Duty Free (CTG, Hainan-centric duty-free monopoly) is at p_fcf ~16 with EPS -16% and revenue -5%, and sits near its 52wk low (proximity ~4%). Against Avolta, Lotte and Shilla it has far higher gross margin (33%), ROIC (13%) and a net-cash balance (Altman Z 4.5), so it screens better on quality than any global travel-retail peer. The derating is driven by Hainan consumption weakness and discount-driven competition; valuation is in line to slightly rich on current earnings but cheap on normalized margins. Mispricing case depends on a Chinese consumption recovery.
1880.HK.rationale: FMP profile confirms China Tourism Group Duty Free Corporation Limited (Sanya, duty-free retail).

1928.HK.relative_comps: Sands China (Macau operations of Las Vegas Sands) trades at p_fcf ~7 with DCF MoS 66% versus Wynn Macau, MGM China, Galaxy Entertainment and SJM, which sit on 8-14x FCF. Gross margin ~79% and net margin 12% are comparable; ROIC 4.4% is low as a result of heavy Cotai capex, and revenue growth 5% is slower than the post-reopening 3y CAGR. Price is near its 52wk high, so market already discounts GGR recovery. Modestly cheap vs Macau peers but the discount is partly justified by the 2023-26 capex burden and Altman Z 1.7 leverage.
1928.HK.rationale: Sands China Ltd, HK-listed Macau integrated-resort operator, subsidiary of Las Vegas Sands.

2020.HK.relative_comps: Anta Sports (Anta, FILA, Descente, Amer Sports stake) trades at p_fcf ~10.7 with 62% gross and 17% net margin, ROIC 14%, versus Li Ning, Xtep and Nike/Adidas/Puma. Revenue +13% beats Nike (flat/neg) and Chinese peers, while valuation is in line to cheaper than Nike's high-teens FCF multiple. Price sits mid 52wk range, below its 200d SMA, so trend is soft after China consumer weakness. Best-in-class quality at a modest discount; the gap is mostly justified by China exposure, but quality-adjusted this is cheap.
2020.HK.rationale: Anta Sports Products, Chinese sportswear leader; global and Chinese athletic apparel are the real comps.

2333.HK.relative_comps: Great Wall Motor (Haval SUVs, ORA, Tank, Wey) trades at p_fcf ~1.5, the lowest in the group, with 82% DCF and 48% EPV MoS. Revenue +10% and 3y CAGR 17% are below Geely and Chery but positive; EPS -22% and net margin 4.5% show margin compression from the price war. Price is at its 52wk high (proximity ~0%), so the market already sees it. A sub-2x FCF multiple likely reflects working-capital and payables funding rather than real cash profit, so verify cash quality before calling it a mispricing.
2333.HK.rationale: Great Wall Motor Company, Baoding-based Chinese SUV/pickup OEM, HK-listed H-share.

6690.HK.relative_comps: Haier Smart Home (Haier/Casarte/GE Appliances/Fisher & Paykel) trades at p_fcf ~9.5, with 27% gross, 6.5% net margin and ROIC 12%. Versus Midea and Gree (premium multiples, higher margins), Whirlpool and Electrolux (low-single-digit-to-teens FCF, lower ROIC), it is in line to cheap. Revenue +6%, EPS +4% show steady but unspectacular growth; price sits ~26% above its 52wk low. Global diversification via GE Appliances justifies a discount to Midea but not a deep one.
6690.HK.rationale: Haier Smart Home Co, Qingdao-based global white goods maker, H-share listing.

9618.HK.relative_comps: JD.com trades at p_fcf ~56 on depressed FCF (EPS -52% from food-delivery and new-business investment) and gross margin 16%, net margin 1.5%, ROIC 3.9%. Against Alibaba, PDD, Meituan and Amazon it looks rich on trailing FCF but cheap on normalized 1P retail profit (EPV MoS slightly negative, DCF MoS 48%). Revenue +10% is steady; price trades well below the 200d SMA. The earnings dislocation is real and deliberate subsidy spending, so the gap is justified near-term; mispricing depends on delivery losses fading.
9618.HK.rationale: JD.com Inc, Chinese 1P e-commerce and logistics, HK secondary listing 9618.

9927.HK.relative_comps: Seres Group (AITO co-development with Huawei, HIMA alliance; HK listing 9927) trades at p_fcf ~1.7 with 85% DCF MoS and revenue 3y CAGR 69%, yet ROIC is negative (-7%) and net margin 3.6%. Price is near its 52wk high. Versus Li Auto, Xpeng, Geely and Great Wall it is cheapest on FCF but has the weakest return on capital and the highest Huawei-dependency risk. Low FCF multiple reflects supplier-financed working capital and a newly listed premium story; deeply discounted but quality-poor, so only partly a mispricing.
9927.HK.rationale: Seres Group, Chongqing Huawei-aligned NEV maker; 9927.HK identified from its profile (price/market cap) and 2025 H-share listing, moderate confidence.

9973.HK.relative_comps: Chery Automobile (HK listing 9973, 2025 IPO) trades at p_fcf ~8, well above Geely (2.8) and Great Wall (1.5) but with higher DCF MoS 84% and a heavy export mix; gross margin 14% is the lowest of the Chinese OEMs and EPS -93% reflects one-offs and IPO-related items. Price is close to its 52wk high. On FCF it is the richest of the Chinese OEMs but export growth (3y CAGR 47%) offsets; in line on a quality-adjusted view.
9973.HK.rationale: Chery Automobile Co, Wuhu-based Chinese OEM with large export business; ticker 9973.HK mapped from 2025 HK IPO and market cap, moderate confidence.

ANF.relative_comps: Abercrombie & Fitch trades at p_fcf ~19 with 61% gross, 9.6% net margin and ROIC 14%, versus American Eagle, Urban Outfitters and Gap which carry lower margins and 8-12x FCF multiples. Revenue +6% and 3y CAGR 12.5% beat AEO and Gap, but EPS is flat to slightly down. Price sits mid-to-upper range of its 52wk band and below the 200d SMA. Premium to apparel-retail peers is partly justified by the best margins in the group; the EPV MoS of -63% says the market is already pricing sustained peak margins.
ANF.rationale: Abercrombie & Fitch Co, US specialty apparel retailer (Abercrombie, Hollister).

APOTEA.ST.relative_comps: Apotea (Swedish online pharmacy, ST-listed) shows p_fcf ~89 which is the richest in the group, with 27% gross, 3.2% net margin but very high ROIC (87%, asset-light with negative working capital). Versus Redcare Pharmacy (premium on growth) and Zur Rose, it trades at a comparable premium; revenue +10% is below Redcare's 20%+. The multi-method MoS values are all -100% (no DCF support) which means the multiple depends on continued growth. Price is near its 52wk high; premium is partly justified by returns but leaves little margin of safety.
APOTEA.ST.rationale: Apotea AB, Nordic e-commerce pharmacy; name mapped from the .ST suffix and Specialty Retail classification, moderate confidence.

BETS-B.ST.relative_comps: Betsson AB (Stockholm-listed online casino and sportsbook operator) trades at p_fcf ~8 with 62% DCF, 43% EPV and 82% Graham MoS, ROIC 18% and net margin 15%. Versus Flutter, Entain, Evoke and Kindred it is the cheapest on FCF while having comparable or better margins and returns; Flutter is on 20x+. Revenue +8% and 3y CAGR 15% are solid. Price is near the lower half of its 52wk range. Consistently cheap on every method, though regulatory tax risk (Sweden, LatAm) justifies some discount.
BETS-B.ST.rationale: Betsson AB B-shares, Swedish online gaming group.

BKNG.relative_comps: Booking Holdings trades at p_fcf ~14 with 20% net margin and ROIC 33%, versus Expedia (~8-10x FCF but lower margins and ROIC), Airbnb (high-20s multiple) and Trip.com. Revenue +13% and 3y CAGR 16% are best-in-class among online travel agencies. Price sits ~18% under its 52wk high. EPV MoS of -100% reflects its asset-light, buyback-driven value, while DCF 31% shows moderate upside. Premium to Expedia is justified by quality and scale; fairly priced rather than mispriced.
BKNG.rationale: Booking Holdings, global online travel agency (Booking.com, Priceline, Kayak).

BYD.relative_comps: Boyd Gaming (US regional casino operator, NYSE ticker BYD, not the Chinese automaker) trades at p_fcf ~16 with 42% gross and a reported 45% net margin (distorted by the FanDuel stake sale gain; EPS +264% is non-recurring). ROIC 12%, revenue +4% and the weakness of EPV MoS (-79%) indicates the valuation depends on the one-off. Versus Red Rock, Churchill Downs, Penn and Caesars it is in line to modestly cheaper on FCF with better returns than Caesars. Price is mid-range for 52wk. No clear mispricing once the gain is stripped out.
BYD.rationale: NYSE BYD verified as Boyd Gaming via the Gambling, Resorts & Casinos industry tag and US pricing, not BYD Co (1211.HK).

CDI.PA.relative_comps: Christian Dior SE (holding company controlling LVMH, ~42% direct stake) screens at p_fcf ~5 and DCF MoS 63%, versus LVMH and Hermes at much higher multiples and Kering/Burberry at lower. Dior SE trades at a structural holding-company discount to look-through LVMH value; gross margin 66%, net margin 5.6% and ROIC 12% are the consolidated LVMH group figures with minority-interest drag. Revenue -4.6% and EPS -13% reflect the luxury downturn. The discount to NAV is persistent and not a fundamental mispricing; cheap vs peers only by holdco logic.
CDI.PA.rationale: Christian Dior SE, Arnault-family holding that consolidates LVMH; peers are LVMH and luxury groups.

CEC.DE.relative_comps: Ceconomy (MediaMarkt and Saturn, ordinary shares, JD.com takeover offer context) trades at p_fcf ~3.2 and 77% DCF MoS with 15% gross margin and ~0 net margin, versus Fnac Darty, Currys and Best Buy at 5-9x FCF. ROIC 1.8% is weak, revenue +3%. Price is at ~93% of the 52wk high because of the takeover bid, which compresses the upside to the bid price. Cheap on nominal FCF but low-margin electronics retail and the bid cap make the gap largely justified.
CEC.DE.rationale: Ceconomy AG ordinary shares; both CEC and CECV are the same company with different share classes (ordinary vs preference).

CECV.DE.relative_comps: Ceconomy preference shares (same MediaMarkt/Saturn business as CEC.DE) trade at p_fcf ~3 with 73% DCF MoS and identical 15% gross and ~0 net margin; ROIC is slightly negative on this record. At its 52wk high, the share is priced for the takeover, while Fnac Darty and Currys trade at 5-9x FCF. Essentially the same story as the ordinary shares, with the preference-share discount to ordinary being the only relative-value driver. In line on fundamentals; upside mostly depends on the bid.
CECV.DE.rationale: Ceconomy AG preferred shares, identified by the CECV.DE suffix and the identical margin figures as CEC.DE.

CHWY.relative_comps: Chewy trades at p_fcf ~17 with 30% gross margin, 1.8% net margin and ROIC 4.7%, versus Walmart and Amazon (premium multiples), Tractor Supply and Petco. Revenue +6% is slower than its history, EPS -43%, and DCF MoS -9% and EPV -100% indicate no valuation cushion. Price is ~26% above its 52wk low, trend still below the 200d. The premium to Petco and Pets at Home is justified by autoship revenue quality, but on margins and ROIC it is rich on trailing numbers.
CHWY.rationale: Chewy Inc, US online pet retailer; peers are pet specialty and online retail.

CURY.L.relative_comps: Currys trades at p_fcf ~6x with strong DCF/owner-earnings MoS, but ROIC is ~2% and net margin 1.8%, so the discount reflects thin economics. Against Fnac Darty (p_fcf 2.4x, 3% ROIC) it is dearer on FCF; versus Best Buy and JB Hi-Fi it is cheaper but lower quality. Growth is flat (3y CAGR -1%), EPS rebound from a low base. Mostly a justified low-margin electronics-retail discount.
CURY.L.rationale: Low-margin consumer-electronics big-box retailer (UK/Nordics); Fnac Darty and Ceconomy are the nearest European analogues.

DBC.WA.relative_comps: Identified as Debica (Polish tyre maker, Goodyear subsidiary); p_fcf is 0 in the data (no FCF reading), so valuation rests on a Graham MoS of ~80% alone, with other methods at -1 (no reading). Gross margin 5.5% and ROIC 7% are poor versus Michelin/Pirelli; revenue +16% y/y is a rebound. Controlled-subsidiary free float and captive Goodyear sourcing mean peer multiples transfer poorly. Treat the cheapness as unproven.
DBC.WA.rationale: Debica S.A. is a Goodyear-controlled Polish tyre manufacturer; peers are global tyre makers. Low confidence on valuation because FCF data is missing.

DECK.relative_comps: DECK at p_fcf ~11.5x with 58% gross margin, 19% net margin and 29% ROIC is the highest-quality name in this group; multi-method MoS is mixed (DCF +41%, EPV -23%, Graham +67%). It sits in the lower part of its 52wk range (0.21), at a lower multiple than ONON/BIRK and better margins and growth than Nike (rev +10%, 3y CAGR 15%). The discount reflects HOKA deceleration and UGG fashion-cycle fears; cheap to in-line.
DECK.rationale: Premium footwear brand owner (HOKA, UGG); peers are branded footwear and apparel with similar margin structure.

DNLM.L.relative_comps: Dunelm: p_fcf ~7.9x, gross margin 53%, ROIC 33%, DCF and owner-earnings MoS ~60%, EPV flat. Revenue growth is low (+3%) and EPS flat; price in the lower part of its range (0.39). Versus Kingfisher (low ROIC) and Wayfair (unprofitable) it earns clearly superior returns at a lower multiple; the discount is driven by UK discretionary/housing sentiment, not business quality.
DNLM.L.rationale: UK homewares/furniture specialist; peers are home improvement and home furnishing retailers.

DUNI.ST.relative_comps: Duni (napkins, tableware, meal packaging for hospitality) trades at p_fcf ~16x with only 5% ROIC, 4% net margin and low growth (+1.4% rev). DCF/Graham MoS are positive (~40-77%) but EPV only 10%. Price is at its 52wk low area (0.02), so momentum is weak. Versus Huhtamaki and other packaging peers it is not cheaper on FCF; the MoS comes from model assumptions rather than a clear mispricing.
DUNI.ST.rationale: Nordic hospitality/consumer packaging and tableware; sector tag Packaging & Containers, peers are specialty packaging.

EVO.ST.relative_comps: Evolution (live-casino B2B supplier): p_fcf ~13x with 50% net margin and 23% ROIC, far above operator peers (Flutter, Entain at ~5-10% margins); revenue slightly negative y/y (-4%) after a 13% 3y CAGR. Price near its 52wk high (0.90). EPV MoS -44% flags that earnings power is already priced; DCF/Graham positive. Cheap on FCF relative to quality, but growth has stalled and regulatory risk is high.
EVO.ST.rationale: Live-dealer casino content supplier to online operators; peers are B2B gaming suppliers and online gambling groups.

FNAC.PA.relative_comps: Fnac Darty: p_fcf ~2.4x, MoS very high on DCF/EPV/owner-earnings (60-76%), but ROIC 3%, net margin slightly negative and Altman Z 1.5 signals fragility. Revenue +25% y/y looks like M&A (Unieuro) rather than organic growth. Price near 52wk high (0.89) so the market has already rerated it. Cheaper than Currys and Best Buy on FCF; the discount is partly justified by weak margins and balance sheet.
FNAC.PA.rationale: French/Iberian electronics and cultural-goods retailer; closest are Currys, Ceconomy, Best Buy.

FR.PA.relative_comps: Valeo: p_fcf ~5.3x vs 1-3x for Forvia/OPmobility with similarly thin economics (gross 15%, net margin 1%, ROIC 4%, Altman Z 1.3). Multi-method MoS is mostly negative (DCF -13%, EPV -53%, Graham -61%), unlike peers whose models are positive. Price in the lower range (0.23). Cheaper than Aptiv/Lear/Magna, but within the screened European auto-supplier set it is the dearest and has the weakest model support.
FR.PA.rationale: Valeo SA, French Tier-1 auto supplier (lighting, driver assistance, thermal); verified by auto-parts industry and French listing.

FRVIA.PA.relative_comps: Forvia: p_fcf 0.8x (extreme), DCF MoS +78%, but revenue -21% y/y (divestments), net margin -10%, Altman Z 0.78 (distress zone), and price near 52wk low (0.06). Heavily indebted after the Faurecia/Hella deal. The deep discount to Valeo/OPmobility looks mostly justified by leverage and negative earnings; a mispricing only if deleveraging succeeds.
FRVIA.PA.rationale: Forvia SE (Faurecia+Hella), French Tier-1 supplier of seating, interiors, lighting and electronics; leveraged.

GAW.L.relative_comps: Games Workshop (Warhammer): p_fcf ~25.5x, 72% gross margin, 31% net margin, 51% ROIC, Altman Z 30: best-in-class unit economics with growth (+7% rev, 12% 3y CAGR). Multi-method MoS is mostly negative (DCF -17%, EPV -100%), so the stock is priced for perfection; price at 0.15 of the 52wk range. Rich against Hasbro and Mattel on FCF, but the quality gap largely supports the premium.
GAW.L.rationale: Owner of the Warhammer IP and vertically integrated miniatures manufacturer-retailer; peers are IP-driven hobby/toy and games companies.

GIII.relative_comps: G-III (licensed and owned apparel, Calvin Klein/Tommy Hilfiger licenses): p_fcf ~5.4x with DCF MoS +74% and EPV +31%; but gross 38%, net 2%, ROIC 9%, revenue -7% y/y and EPS -64%. Cheaper than PVH/RL/Tapestry on FCF but earnings are falling and license concentration risk is large. Mid-range price (0.56). The discount is partly deserved.
GIII.rationale: Apparel manufacturer with major licenses (Calvin Klein, Tommy Hilfiger, DKNY) and owned brands; peers are branded apparel groups.

GNTX.relative_comps: Gentex (auto-dimming mirrors): p_fcf ~9.1x, gross 34%, net 15%, ROIC 16%, Altman Z 7.6, net cash. Growth is decent (+10% rev, 3y CAGR 10%) but EPS flat. Price at its 52wk low (0.00), a negative trend. Margins and returns far above most auto suppliers (Lear, Magna) at a similar or lower multiple; DCF MoS 32%, Graham 68%, EPV -17%. Looks cheap versus peers despite weak momentum.
GNTX.rationale: US auto-electronics niche leader (dimming mirrors, driver-monitoring); the sector tag Auto - Parts fits.

GRG.L.relative_comps: Greggs: p_fcf ~33x, gross 61% (vertical bakery-retail), net 5.7%, ROIC 15%, rev +6.8% with 12% 3y CAGR but EPS -21%; price near 52wk high (0.96). DCF -100%, owner earnings -100%, Graham -81%. Rich against UK pub/restaurant peers on FCF; the returns do not warrant 33x FCF given the earnings decline. A real valuation stretch, not just a quality premium.
GRG.L.rationale: UK bakery-led food-to-go retailer; peers are UK/global quick-service and food-to-go chains.

INCH.L.relative_comps: Inchcape (global distributor for premium auto brands): p_fcf ~7.3x with DCF +61%, EPV +46%, owner earnings +59%, Graham +52%; gross 16.5%, net margin 3%, ROIC 10%. Revenue -2% y/y, EPS -29%. Price at the lower end (0.16). Cheaper than US dealers (Penske, Lithia) with similar returns; the discount reflects EM/currency exposure and falling EPS, but the gap looks bigger than fundamentals justify.
INCH.L.rationale: Global automotive distribution and retail (Toyota, JLR, Subaru markets); closest listed peers are large dealer/distribution groups.

JD.L.relative_comps: JD Sports: p_fcf ~4.8x, gross 47%, net 3.4%, ROIC 8%, rev +10.5% (acquisition-fueled), EPS -10%. DCF +47%, EPV +35%, Graham +80%, owner earnings +64%. Price near 52wk high (0.85), momentum strong. Cheaper than Dick's, Next and Foot Locker on FCF with comparable returns; the discount reflects Nike dependence and acquisitive capital allocation.
JD.L.rationale: UK-based global sports-fashion retailer; peers are athletic and fashion specialty retailers.

JET2.L.relative_comps: Jet2 (UK package holidays + charter airline): p_fcf ~6x, DCF +77%, EPV +36%, Graham +85%, gross 11.6%, net 5.5%, ROIC 6%. Rev +4%, 3y CAGR 14%, EPS flat. Price in the upper range (0.84). Cheaper than Ryanair/easyJet on FCF, but customer-deposit float inflates FCF. Moderately cheap versus peers.
JET2.L.rationale: UK leisure airline and package-holiday operator; closest peers are European leisure carriers and TUI.

MMB.PA.relative_comps: Identified as Lagardere SA (travel retail, Hachette publishing, media); p_fcf ~2.7x, DCF +72%, owner earnings +75%, EPV +54%; low gross margin 7% (distorted by conglomerate/retail mix), net 2%, ROIC 6%, Altman Z 1.3. Price mid-range (0.43). Cheap against Avolta and WH Smith on FCF, but controlling-shareholder dynamics and conglomerate accounting distort the screen. Cheap on paper, low confidence.
MMB.PA.rationale: Lagardere SA (MMB.PA) is a French travel-retail/publishing conglomerate; peers chosen on its travel-retail core. Identity moderately confident; not verified from universe data (no company name field).

OPM.PA.relative_comps: OPmobility (ex-Plastic Omnium; fuel systems, exteriors, lighting): p_fcf ~3.0x, DCF +37%, EPV +38%, Graham +53%, owner earnings +53%; gross 9.4%, net 1.8%, ROIC 6%. Rev -2.6%, EPS +10%, price close to 52wk low (0.04). Cheaper than Valeo with positive models and less leverage than Forvia; thin margins are sector-typical. Looks cheap versus European auto-supplier peers.
OPM.PA.rationale: OPmobility (formerly Plastic Omnium), French Tier-1 in fuel systems, exteriors and lighting.

PAH3.DE.relative_comps: Porsche Automobil Holding SE is a holding company whose value is its Volkswagen stake and a small Porsche AG stake; reported gross/net margin ~100% and negative ROIC reflect equity-method accounting, so operating ratios and p_fcf (10.7x) are not meaningful. Price at 52wk low (0.01); DCF/Graham MoS positive, EPV and owner earnings -1. The right comparison is the NAV discount to look-through VW/Porsche stakes, where it is typically cheap, but it is not comparable to auto OEMs.
PAH3.DE.rationale: Holding company, not an operator; peers are listed holding companies and the underlying VW/Porsche AG. Operating screens are not valid here.

PDD.relative_comps: PDD (Pinduoduo/Temu): p_fcf ~7.4x, gross 56%, net 23%, ROIC 19%, revenue +9.7% y/y (decelerating from a 49% 3y CAGR), EPS -14%. All methods positive (DCF +67%, EPV +34%, Graham +83%). Price at the low end of its range (0.12). Higher margins and returns than JD/Alibaba/MELI at a lower FCF multiple; the discount reflects tariff/de minimis risk on Temu, China governance and slowing growth. Cheap versus peers.
PDD.rationale: Chinese e-commerce/social commerce platform (Pinduoduo, Temu); peers are large e-commerce platforms.

RL.relative_comps: Ralph Lauren (Apparel - Manufacturers, 70% gross margin, 11.6% net margin, 12% ROIC) trades at ~32x P/FCF, the richest of its set; Tapestry is at ~15x with a higher net margin (19%) and ROIC (15%), and PVH/Capri/Levi's sit at low-to-mid-teens or distressed multiples. The multi-method MoS spread is negative on DCF (-64%), owner earnings (-70%) and EPV (-100%), with only Graham positive, so the market is paying for brand durability rather than cash yield. Growth is real (revenue +14.6%, EPS +30%) and the stock is 66% of the way up its 52-week range, near its 200-day average, so the premium is partly justified by brand quality, but it leaves little margin for error versus peers. Verdict: rich versus peers, with the premium only partly earned.
RL.rationale: Ralph Lauren is a global lifestyle and apparel brand across wholesale, DTC and licensing. The true comparables are the American premium accessible-luxury and heritage brands (Tapestry, Capri, PVH, Levi's) and the European luxury houses (LVMH, Hermes, Kering, Richemont) as the aspirational valuation anchor.

TPR.relative_comps: Tapestry (Coach, Kate Spade) has the best cash-flow valuation in its set at ~15x P/FCF with a 78% gross margin, 19% net margin and 15% ROIC, against Ralph Lauren at ~32x. Revenue (+14%) and EPS growth (+787%, a rebound from depressed prior-year earnings) are strong, but the EPS figure overstates run-rate growth because of the base effect. MoS is mixed (Graham +42%, DCF -13%, owner earnings -32%, EPV -100%), and the stock sits mid-range (50% of its 52-week range) with price modestly below its 200-day average, a neutral-to-soft trend signal. Cheap versus accessible-luxury peers and not obviously a value trap, though the multi-method spread is not decisively positive.
TPR.rationale: Tapestry is a US accessible-luxury handbag and accessories group (Coach, Kate Spade). Its closest comparables are Ralph Lauren, Capri (Michael Kors, Versace), PVH and Levi's in the US premium segment, plus the European luxury houses (LVMH, Kering, Richemont) and Burberry as higher-multiple references.

VC.relative_comps: Visteon (digital cockpit electronics and displays for automakers) trades at ~8x P/FCF, cheaper than most auto-parts peers, with strong MoS signals on DCF (+43%), owner earnings (+51%) and Graham (+78%), though EPV is negative (-16%). Fundamentals are the weak spot: revenue -2.5%, EPS -26%, a 14% gross margin and 5% net margin, with ROIC of ~9%, so it ranks below Aptiv and Gentex on quality and growth. The stock is only 22% up its 52-week range and well below its 200-day average, a clear downtrend. The discount is partly justified by shrinking earnings and OEM concentration, but the cash-flow gap versus peers suggests some real mispricing if cockpit-electronics volumes stabilise.
VC.rationale: Visteon (VC) is a Tier-1 automotive supplier of digital instrument clusters, infotainment and cockpit domain controllers. Real peers are cockpit and electronics suppliers (Aptiv, Gentex, Continental and Forvia's electronics unit) and broader auto-parts names such as Lear, Adient and BorgWarner.

VRLA.PA.relative_comps: Verallia (Paris, EUR) is the European glass-packaging leader; it trades at ~11x P/FCF with a very positive multi-method spread (owner earnings +63%, DCF +45%, EPV +8%, Graham -5%). Margins are thin (17% gross, 2.7% net) and ROIC is ~11%, with revenue -3.6% and EPS -61%, which reflects volume destocking and energy-cost normalisation in the glass cycle. Altman Z is a low 1.7, so leverage is the main caveat versus Vidrala and Amcor, which carry stronger balance sheets. The stock is near the bottom of its 52-week range and below its 200-day average. Cheap versus packaging peers on cash flow, with the discount partly explained by earnings decline and leverage, but the MoS spread suggests meaningful mispricing if the cycle turns.
VRLA.PA.rationale: VRLA.PA is Verallia SA, a Paris-listed maker of glass bottles and jars for wine, spirits, beer and food. Its true comparables are Vidrala (Spain), O-I Glass, Vetropack (Switzerland) and Gerresheimer/Verescence in pharma and cosmetics glass, plus broader rigid-packaging names such as Amcor, Berry Global and Ardagh.

WHR.relative_comps: Whirlpool trades at ~18x P/FCF with every intrinsic-value method negative or at the floor (DCF -100%, owner earnings -100%, EPV -100%, Graham -19%), so on this data it is not cheap despite trading near its 52-week low (only 5% up its range, far below the 200-day average). Fundamentals are the weakest in the set: revenue -6.5% (3-year CAGR -7.7%), flat EPS, 15% gross margin, 2% net margin, ROIC ~10% and an Altman Z of 1.2 in the distress zone. Versus Electrolux, Haier/Midea and SharkNinja the multiple is not a discount to quality; the stock is deeply oversold, but the cash-flow-based gap is not a mispricing signal. Rich relative to its earnings power and balance-sheet risk, with the weak price action reflecting real deterioration.
WHR.rationale: Whirlpool (WHR) is the largest US maker of major home appliances (washers, refrigerators, ranges) with brands Whirlpool, KitchenAid and Maytag. True peers are Electrolux, Haier/GE Appliances, Midea, LG, Samsung and Bosch (BSH) in major appliances, plus SharkNinja and Helen of Troy for small appliances.

0763.HK.relative_comps: At ~41x p_fcf with 30% gross and 4% net margin, ZTE is rich on cash flow against Ericsson/Nokia (mid-teens p_fcf, similar margins) though DCF/owner-earnings MoS is mildly positive. Growth (+10% rev) beats the telecom-equipment group but EPS fell 34% and ROIC is 7%. Trades near the 52-wk low zone and below sma200; the discount is partly justified by China-carrier capex exposure and margin dilution from servers/AI.
0763.HK.rationale: Chinese telecom network equipment plus servers; direct global comps are Ericsson/Nokia/Huawei.

2382.HK.relative_comps: Sunny at ~19x p_fcf with 20% gross, 11% net margin and +13% revenue / +71% EPS growth is in line to modestly cheap versus Largan and AAC; Graham MoS is strongly positive but other methods are not. ROIC 8% is low. Lower-middle of the 52-wk range (0.40) and below sma200, so trend is weak.
2382.HK.rationale: Optical lens/camera modules, vehicle optics; peers are Asian optical and precision component makers.

3986.HK.relative_comps: At ~151x p_fcf GigaDevice is far richer than Winbond/Macronix (memory cyclicals, roughly 15-30x FCF) and MCU peers; growth (+20% rev, +49% EPS) and 37% gross margin justify some premium but not this much. Price is only 7% above the 52-wk-range low-end measure yet well below sma200 after a huge swing; every MoS method reads -1.
3986.HK.rationale: NOR flash, MCU and DRAM fabless chip designer (HK listing of Shanghai-listed GigaDevice); peers are memory/MCU designers.

6809.HK.relative_comps: Montage at ~100x p_fcf is rich versus Rambus (~25-30x) but its 60% gross, 41% net margin and +46% revenue growth align more with Astera Labs/Credo, which also trade at premium multiples. Fundamentals are excellent but the multiple already discounts AI-server memory-interface (DDR5 RCD, PCIe retimer) growth; all MoS methods negative and ROIC only 10%. Price far below sma200 and near the low end of its range.
6809.HK.rationale: Memory-interface and server connectivity chips for DDR5/AI servers; peers are Rambus, Astera Labs, Credo.

ADBE.relative_comps: At ~10.5x p_fcf with 89% gross, 30% net margin, 27% ROIC and +10% revenue growth, Adobe is clearly cheap versus Intuit/Autodesk/Salesforce (typically 20-30x FCF); DCF MoS +35% and Graham +63% confirm. The discount reflects generative-AI disruption fear (Canva, Figma, Firefly competition); price is 31% up from the 52-wk low but below sma200, trend weak. Growth is slowing but not collapsing, so the gap looks like a partly real mispricing.
ADBE.rationale: Creative/document software; direct competitors Canva, Figma, Autodesk, Microsoft; seat-based SaaS peers.

AMKR.relative_comps: AMKR at ~47x p_fcf is rich versus ASE (~15-20x) because FCF is depressed by heavy capex; 14% gross, 6% net margin, ROIC 10% and +6% revenue are ordinary OSAT economics. DCF MoS -68%, all else -1. Price sits near the low end of its 52-wk range (0.09) and under sma200, so the AI-packaging premium has faded.
AMKR.rationale: US OSAT: semiconductor assembly and test; peers are ASE, JCET, PTI.

AOF.DE.relative_comps: Atoss at ~30x p_fcf with 77% gross, 26% net margin and 40% ROIC is in line with quality vertical SaaS (Workday/Dayforce roughly 20-30x FCF); growth +11% is steady and Graham MoS +22% positive. Price is in the lower half of the 52-wk range (0.38) and below sma200. Premium ROIC supports the multiple.
AOF.DE.rationale: German workforce management software (time and attendance, scheduling); peers are WFM/HCM vendors.

BOUV.OL.relative_comps: Bouvet at ~17x p_fcf with 20% gross, 9% net margin and ROIC 42% is in line to slightly rich versus Nordic IT-consulting peers (Knowit, Tietoevry, Netcompany, roughly 10-18x); revenue flat (-0.2%) and EPS -6%, so growth does not justify a premium. DCF MoS +57% looks generous. Price mid-range (0.50), below sma200.
BOUV.OL.rationale: Norwegian IT consultancy; peers are Nordic/European IT services firms.

DAVE.relative_comps: Dave at ~14x p_fcf with 87% gross, 35% net margin and +60% revenue / +223% EPS growth looks cheap versus SoFi/Upstart/Affirm (higher multiples on lower profitability). ROIC is negative, reflecting a funding-heavy balance sheet; the stock is 41% up from its 52-wk low yet well below sma200. Growth exceeds peers so the discount is mostly a real gap, though credit-loss and CAC risks persist.
DAVE.rationale: US neobank with cash-advance products; peers are consumer fintech lenders.

EEFT.relative_comps: Euronet at ~7.5x p_fcf with 7% net margin and ROIC 8% is cheaper than Global Payments/Fiserv/Wise (10-20x) and near Western Union (~5-6x but declining); DCF +61%, Graham +74%, EPV +10% all positive. Growth is steady (+6% rev/eps); the discount reflects low ROIC, goodwill-heavy balance sheet (Altman 2.1) and a flat stock below sma200 (0.51 of range). A moderate real mispricing.
EEFT.rationale: ATM/EFT, money transfer (Ria, Xe) and epay; peers are payments and remittance firms.

EFOR.relative_comps: Not assessed: the identity of ticker EFOR could not be confirmed, so no peer set or relative ranking is given.
EFOR.rationale: Unmapped: I do not confidently recognize EFOR and will not guess a peer set from ticker letters; data shows an IT-services profile with shrinking revenue but the identity is unverified.

FICO.relative_comps: FICO at ~15x p_fcf with 86% gross, 33% net margin, 47% ROIC and +27% revenue growth is cheap versus bureaus (EFX/TRU roughly 25-30x FCF) and MCO/SPGI; Graham +49%, iv15 +46% MoS. Price is only 10% above the 52-wk low and far below sma200 after the pricing/VantageScore scare, so the gap reflects regulatory pricing-power risk rather than quality; a genuine mispricing if the score franchise holds.
FICO.rationale: Credit scoring and decisioning software; peers are credit bureaus and data/analytics franchises.

FIG.relative_comps: Figma data is blank (p_fcf, margins, growth all zero from a thin scan after its 2025 IPO), so quantitative ranking is not possible. The stock is 12% above its 52-wk low and well under sma200 after a large drawdown from IPO highs; versus Adobe and Atlassian it trades on EV/gross profit with higher growth but richer sales multiples. Treat as unranked on data.
FIG.rationale: Collaborative design/product software; direct comps are Adobe, Canva, Atlassian, Autodesk.

HPQ.relative_comps: HP at ~10x p_fcf with 20% gross, 4.6% net margin and +3% revenue is in line with Dell/Lenovo (roughly 8-12x FCF); DCF +14% and owner earnings +26% modestly positive. ROIC is 29% on a tiny equity base while EPS is -6% and 3y revenue CAGR negative, so the discount is justified by an ex-growth PC/printing mix. Upper half of range (0.63), below sma200.
HPQ.rationale: PC and printer maker; peers are Dell, Lenovo, Canon, Xerox.

IT.relative_comps: Gartner at ~12x p_fcf with 68% gross, 11% net margin and 21% ROIC is cheap versus research/data peers (SPGI/MCO/VRSK roughly 25-30x FCF); DCF +48% and owner earnings +41% MoS positive. EPS fell 40% and revenue growth slowed to 4% on public-sector cuts and AI-substitution fears, which explains part of the discount. Price mid-range (0.51) and below sma200; partially real mispricing.
IT.rationale: IT research and conferences subscription; peers are Forrester, Accenture and data/research franchises.

KD.relative_comps: Kyndryl at ~11.6x p_fcf with 22% gross, 1.3% net margin and flat revenue is similar to DXC/Atos but cheap versus Accenture/Capgemini; EPV +72% and owner earnings +81% MoS are high given the turnaround, yet ROIC is -0.6% and Altman Z 1.3 signals leverage risk. Price is 38% above the 52-wk low and the discount is partly justified by weak margins.
KD.rationale: IBM spin-off managed infrastructure services; peers are DXC, Atos/Eviden, Capgemini, Accenture.

KTN.VI.relative_comps: Kontron at ~19x p_fcf with 12% gross, 9% net margin, +56% EPS but -5% revenue and ROIC 6% is rich versus Eurotech and mixed versus Advantech (higher margins, higher multiple); MoS mixed (owner earnings +16%, others negative). Price in the lower third of its range (0.30), below sma200. Quality is mediocre for the valuation.
KTN.VI.rationale: Austrian embedded/IoT computing and IT services (formerly S&T); peers are industrial computing firms.

LYFT.relative_comps: Lyft at ~6.4x p_fcf with +9% revenue and 41% gross is cheap versus Uber (roughly 15-20x FCF) and DoorDash; reported 45% net margin and +12,000% EPS are a tax-benefit/one-off distortion, Altman Z is negative and ROIC 8%. Graham MoS +71% but EPV/iv15 negative; stock is 35% above lows and below sma200. Discount is largely justified by smaller scale, AV disruption risk and balance-sheet leverage.
LYFT.rationale: US rideshare; peers are Uber, Grab, Didi, DoorDash.

NOD.OL.relative_comps: Nordic at ~62x p_fcf with 15% gross (data oddity) and 2% net margin is rich versus Silicon Labs and Espressif; growth is strong at +31% revenue but EPS flat and all MoS methods are -1. Price is in the upper half of its range (0.64) and still below sma200. Premium reflects BLE/Wi-Fi recovery but is not supported by current cash flow.
NOD.OL.rationale: Norwegian low-power wireless SoC/BLE chips; peers are Silicon Labs, Espressif, ST, Infineon.

PTEC.L.relative_comps: Playtech at ~28x p_fcf looks rich versus Evolution (~15x) and Flutter, but the data are distorted by disposal gains (gross margin >100%, net margin 194%) after the Snaitech sale; revenue -12%, 3y CAGR -22% and ROIC 0.5% indicate shrinking continuing operations. Owner-earnings +80% and Graham +64% MoS are artefacts. Price in upper half of range (0.63), below sma200.
PTEC.L.rationale: B2B iGaming software and live casino supplier; peers are Evolution, Light & Wonder, Kambi, Aristocrat.

SMCI.relative_comps: SMCI is an AI-server assembler with ~11% gross margin and ~6% net margin, in line with ODM/OEM peers (Dell, Quanta, Wiwynn) and far below component vendors. Growth is top of the peer set (rev +78% y/y, EPS +94%) and roic of ~14% is acceptable, but p_fcf of 0.0 is a no-data/negative-FCF default (working-capital burn), so the cash-flow valuation cannot be read. The MoS methods disagree sharply (EPV -50%, DCF -100%, Graham +75%), so there is no consistent cheap signal. The price sits at 23% of its 52-week range and below its sma200, which is weak momentum against AI-hardware peers. The discount reflects margin and governance/accounting risk and looks justified, not a clear mispricing.
SMCI.rationale: Super Micro Computer: GPU/AI rack-scale server builder, competes with Dell/HPE (OEM) and Taiwanese ODMs (Quanta, Wiwynn, Foxconn), with NVDA as supplier/ecosystem anchor. Business model is low-margin assembly with heavy working capital.

SWON.SW.relative_comps: SoftwareONE (Zurich) resells and manages software licences and cloud (Microsoft, AWS) and merged with Crayon. It trades on p_fcf of 6.5x and EPV MoS of +50%, which is much cheaper than Softcat, Computacenter, Bechtle or CDW, whose FCF multiples run mid-teens or higher. The reasons for the gap are weak quality markers: net margin of ~0.1%, ROIC of ~11%, an Altman Z of 0.5 and zero EPS growth despite +22% revenue, likely from merger integration and leverage. The price is at 69% of its 52-week range and just below its sma200. This looks cheap on cash flow but part of the discount is justified by thin profit conversion and balance-sheet risk. It is a real mispricing only if the merger synergies deliver.
SWON.SW.rationale: SoftwareONE Holding AG (Swiss-listed, .SW): software licensing reseller and cloud services provider, merged with Crayon. True comps are IT distributors and VARs (CDW, Insight, Softcat, Computacenter, Bechtle, Crayon, Cancom), not software developers, even though the screen labels it Technology Distributors.

TRST.L.relative_comps: Trustpilot (UK online review marketplace, SaaS subscriptions to businesses) has a 78% gross margin and revenue +26% / EPS +31%, which is faster growth than Yelp, Tripadvisor or Angi. Net margin is ~3% and ROIC ~2.5%, so profitability is still immature compared to Auto Trader and Rightmove (very high margins). At 25.5x p_fcf it is not cheap; it is in line with or above Yelp (~10-15x) and below the quality platforms (Auto Trader ~25-30x). All the MoS methods are at or below -30% because there is little earnings power yet. The price is 81% of its 52-week high, so momentum is intact. The multiple looks supported by growth but not obviously mispriced.
TRST.L.rationale: Trustpilot Group plc (LSE): consumer review platform monetised through business subscriptions. Closest comps are online review/lead-generation marketplaces (Yelp, Tripadvisor, Angi) and UK classified platforms (Auto Trader, Rightmove) for model quality.

UPBD.relative_comps: Upbound (formerly Rent-A-Center) is a rent-to-own and lease-to-own retailer/fintech, not software despite the screen's industry label. At p_fcf of 6.2x and EPV MoS of +86% / owner-earnings MoS of +92%, it is cheap against PROG, FirstCash and Affirm, and comparable with Aaron's. Growth is modest (rev +9%, EPS -43%) and net margin ~1.6% with ROIC ~4.6% is weak, reflecting leverage and credit/lease-loss costs. Price is at 96% of its 52-week range, above the sma200, so momentum is strong. The discount to peers is partly justified by low returns on capital and subprime exposure, but the cash-flow yield makes it a mispricing candidate if the earnings recover.
UPBD.rationale: Upbound Group Inc (UPBD): rent-to-own operator (Rent-A-Center, Acima, Brigit). The FMP industry label 'Software - Application' is a mis-map; the real peers are lease-to-own and consumer-finance/pawn businesses.

VRSN.relative_comps: Verisign operates the .com/.net registries as a regulated near-monopoly with an 88% gross margin and ~50% net margin, which is far above any peer (GoDaddy, Tucows, Akamai). At 27x p_fcf with revenue +6% and EPS +10% it is richer than GoDaddy and Akamai on cash flow, but it carries near-zero reinvestment needs and capped price escalators. The negative ROIC (-122) and negative Altman Z are artefacts of negative book equity from buybacks, not distress. Price is at 90% of its 52-week range. A premium to the peer group is justified by margin and moat quality, but slow growth caps the upside, so it is fairly valued rather than cheap.
VRSN.rationale: VeriSign Inc: sole registry operator for .com and .net under ICANN/US Commerce contract. No direct competitor; closest economics are domain/registry and internet-infrastructure toll franchises (GoDaddy, Tucows, CentralNic) plus exchange-like monopolies.

WDC.relative_comps: Western Digital is now a pure-play hard-disk maker (after separating Flash into SanDisk) and competes essentially one-on-one with Seagate in an HDD duopoly. Growth is strong (rev +36%, EPS +374%) with gross margin ~49% and ROIC ~13%, and net margin of 73% is inflated by a one-off gain, so it should not be used for comparison. At 32x p_fcf it is rich against Seagate and Micron, whose cash multiples are lower in the mid-teens to low-twenties, and all MoS methods are at -100%. The price is only 24% of its 52-week range after dropping from a high near $800 and is below its sma200, a fresh crash. The multiple is stretched on trough-like free cash flow, but the crash may already have discounted the cycle, so it is a cyclical rich-on-trailing-numbers name.
WDC.rationale: Western Digital Corp: HDD (data-centre capacity) maker after the SanDisk spin. Direct peer is Seagate; memory/NAND names (Micron, SanDisk, Kioxia) share the AI-storage cycle. Verify screen figures against post-spin segments.

WISE.L.relative_comps: Wise (cross-border payments, UK listing) has a 58% gross margin, ROIC ~16%, net margin ~18% and revenue +13% / EPS +21%, which is higher quality than Western Union and Remitly. P_fcf of 1.2x is a distorted figure because customer-balance float flows through operating cash flow, so cash-flow multiples cannot be compared to PayPal or Adyen. The DCF (+93%) and EPV (+75%) MoS values are high, but they probably capitalise float interest income, which is rate-sensitive. The price is at 40% of its 52-week range, below its sma200, so momentum is weak. Valuation looks cheap against PayPal, Adyen and Remitly on earnings, but the interest-income dependence and price-cut strategy justify part of the gap.
WISE.L.rationale: Wise plc (LSE): international money-transfer and multi-currency account provider. Peers are payments and remittance companies (Remitly, Western Union, PayPal, Adyen, Payoneer, Flywire). Not an IT services company, despite the FMP industry label.

0762.HK.relative_comps: China Unicom (HK) screens cheap at ~6.2x p_fcf with strong EPV and owner-earnings MoS, below China Mobile and China Telecom on cash multiples. Growth is flat (revenue -1.9%, eps -1.5%) and net margin is ~5%, so part of the discount is justified by weaker returns than China Mobile. Price sits near the 52-week low and below SMA200; a modest real discount with state-capex and low-growth caveats.
0762.HK.rationale: China Unicom (Hong Kong): one of the three Chinese state telecom carriers; peers are China Mobile, China Telecom and Asian incumbent telcos.

0788.HK.relative_comps: China Tower trades at ~5.2x p_fcf with strong owner-earnings MoS, far below Western tower REITs. Growth is low single digits, ROIC only ~4% and tenancy is concentrated in three state carriers, so a discount to AMT or Cellnex is warranted. Price near the 52-week low and below SMA200; the gap is mostly a concentration and return-on-capital discount, with some real mispricing.
0788.HK.rationale: China Tower: sole Chinese macro-tower operator anchored by the state carriers; closest comparables are listed tower companies.

1024.HK.relative_comps: Kuaishou at ~7.8x p_fcf with 12.5% revenue growth, 21.6% eps growth and 13% net margin looks cheap against Tencent, Meta and Pinterest. Price is at the 52-week low and far below SMA200, which signals heavy negative sentiment (Douyin competition, China internet de-rating). Gap is partly justified by competitive intensity, but growth plus margin suggest a real discount.
1024.HK.rationale: Kuaishou: Chinese short-video and livestream platform; peers are Tencent, Bilibili, Pinterest, Snap, Meta and Weibo.

1698.HK.relative_comps: The Tencent Music HK line at ~9.4x p_fcf with 12.8% revenue growth, 64% eps growth and a 34% net margin is cheap against Spotify and the labels on cash multiples. Quality is strong, but it is a China-only audio platform with royalty dependence on labels and Tencent, which explains some of the gap. Price is near the 52-week low and below SMA200; modest mispricing.
1698.HK.rationale: 1698.HK is the Hong Kong listing of Tencent Music Entertainment (QQ Music, Kugou, Kuwo); peers are streaming and music-rights names.

9888.HK.relative_comps: Baidu has no usable p_fcf (0.0 default, so unknown), with negative DCF MoS but positive EPV and owner-earnings MoS. Revenue -3%, eps -82% and net margin 4% show a weakening core search and ads business funding AI and cloud. Price is at the 52-week low and well below SMA200; cheap on asset and sum-of-parts, but the earnings trend does not yet justify a rerating.
9888.HK.rationale: Baidu Inc HK secondary line (9888.HK); Chinese internet peers are Tencent, Alibaba, NetEase, Kuaishou, plus Alphabet globally.

CARG.relative_comps: CarGurus at ~11.7x p_fcf with ~89% gross margin and 17% net margin is cheaper than Auto Trader on multiples but with weaker growth (revenue +5%, 3y CAGR negative after the CarOffer wind-down; eps jump is a base effect). DCF MoS is negative and price is mid-range, so it is not obviously mispriced. A discount to Auto Trader is justified by lower market dominance.
CARG.rationale: CarGurus: US online automotive marketplace; peers are Cars.com, TrueCar, Auto Trader Group, Carvana, OPENLANE.

CMCSA.relative_comps: Comcast at ~4.8x p_fcf with strongly positive owner-earnings, Graham and DCF MoS is among the cheapest in the US cable and media set versus Charter, Disney and Verizon. Revenue is flat, broadband subscriber losses and linear TV decline cap the multiple, yet net margin (16%) and eps growth (+30%) are solid. The discount is largely explained by broadband share loss but its magnitude points to genuine cheapness.
CMCSA.rationale: Comcast: cable and broadband, NBCUniversal media and parks, Sky; peers are Charter, Disney, Warner Bros Discovery, AT&T and Verizon.

DJT.relative_comps: Trump Media at ~83x p_fcf with a hugely negative net margin and Altman Z of -2.4 is rich against every social peer, all of which are profitable and far larger. Revenue is tiny and flat; value rests on brand and treasury holdings rather than operations. No valuation method supports the price, and the price is above SMA200 and in the lower part of its 52-week range.
DJT.rationale: DJT: owner of Truth Social with minimal revenue; compared against ad-funded social platforms.

FNTN.DE.relative_comps: freenet at ~7.9x p_fcf with positive EPV, DCF and owner-earnings MoS is cheap versus Deutsche Telekom and 1&1 on cash yield. Revenue is slightly negative and gross margin is ~26% reflecting its reseller and MVNO model, so quality is below network owners. Price is in the lower part of its 52-week range; a small real mispricing supported by a high payout.
FNTN.DE.rationale: freenet AG: German mobile service provider and retailer with waipu.tv IPTV; peers are Telekom, O2 Telefonica Deutschland, 1&1 and United Internet.

FOUR.L.relative_comps: 4imprint at ~11.8x p_fcf with ~54% ROIC and Altman Z of 12.5 is roughly in line with promotional-product and B2B distribution peers. Revenue is flat this year (+0.5%) though the 3y CAGR is 6.4%; net margin 8.4%. High returns justify a premium over the agency label it carries, so it looks fairly priced, mid-range on the 52-week scale.
FOUR.L.rationale: 4imprint Group: US-centric promotional products direct marketer, mislabelled as an advertising agency; true comps are Cimpress, Deluxe, Bunzl and promo-product distributors.

ITV.L.relative_comps: ITV at ~13.9x p_fcf is richer than M6 and ProSieben on cash flow, though DCF and owner-earnings MoS remain positive. eps fell 42% and 3y revenue CAGR is negative, with Studios offsetting a shrinking linear ad base. Thin 13% gross margin and depressed earnings inflate the multiple; roughly in line with the European free-to-air set, not clearly mispriced.
ITV.L.rationale: ITV plc: UK commercial free-to-air broadcaster plus ITV Studios; peers are European FTA broadcasters.

MMT.PA.relative_comps: M6 at ~11.5x p_fcf with positive EPV and owner-earnings MoS and 9.8% net margin is not expensive versus the pan-European FTA group, but revenue (-4%) and eps (-28%) are declining. Price is mid-range on the 52-week scale. The discount is mostly justified by ad-market weakness and structural linear-TV risk, so mispricing is modest at most.
MMT.PA.rationale: Metropole Television (M6 Group): French free-to-air broadcaster; closest peers TF1, ITV, ProSiebenSat.1, Mediaset.

NOS.LS.relative_comps: NOS at ~5.1x p_fcf with revenue +7.5% and 13.5% net margin is cheap versus Proximus, KPN and Orange and growing faster. Price is at the very top of its 52-week range, so the market is already rerating it; DCF and owner-earnings MoS are positive but EPV is negative. A real but closing discount.
NOS.LS.rationale: NOS SGPS: Portuguese converged telecom and cinema operator; peers are European incumbent telcos.

POL.OL.relative_comps: Polaris Media at ~20x p_fcf is rich against Nordic and international publishers, with eps down 99% and a 0.2% net margin. Gross margin of 89% reflects a publisher cost structure. Growth is flat and ROIC ~1.5%; the multiple is inflated by depressed cash flow and the premium looks unjustified. Price is mid-to-upper range.
POL.OL.rationale: Polaris Media: Norwegian regional newspaper and media group; peers are Nordic publishers.

PROX.BR.relative_comps: Proximus at ~7.8x p_fcf with positive Graham and owner-earnings MoS is cheap versus Orange and KPN on cash flow, but the balance sheet is stretched (Altman Z ~0.9), net margin 6.4%, revenue -2% and ROIC 5.7%. The discount reflects weak domestic growth, fibre capex and Belgian regulation; mostly justified with a small real mispricing.
PROX.BR.rationale: Proximus Group: Belgian incumbent telecom plus international carrier business; peers are European incumbents.

RDDT.relative_comps: Reddit at ~29x p_fcf is richer than Meta and Alphabet but growth is far stronger: revenue +69%, 3y CAGR +49%, 91% gross margin and 24% net margin. Price is near the 52-week low and well below SMA200, a deep drawdown after the run-up. Growth justifies a premium; intrinsic-value methods show no MoS, so it is not cheap on those.
RDDT.rationale: Reddit: ad-funded community platform with AI data licensing; peers are Pinterest, Snap, Meta.

RMV.L.relative_comps: Rightmove at ~19x p_fcf with 51% net margin, ~100% gross margin and +9% revenue growth is priced like Auto Trader and REA, a premium justified by exceptional quality. DCF MoS is only 12% and owner-earnings MoS ~1%, so it is fairly valued. Price is near the top of the 52-week range.
RMV.L.rationale: Rightmove: UK online property portal with dominant share; peers are Auto Trader, REA Group, Scout24, Zillow.

RWAY.MI.relative_comps: Rai Way at ~11x p_fcf with 31% net margin and 24% ROIC is in line to slightly cheap versus European tower peers such as INWIT and Cellnex. Growth is modest (+2.4%) and the business is anchored on RAI, so concentration explains part of the discount. Price is near the 52-week low.
RWAY.MI.rationale: Rai Way: Italian broadcast-tower operator majority-owned by RAI; peers are tower infrastructure companies.

SAX.DE.relative_comps: Stroeer at ~6.9x p_fcf with strong owner-earnings and DCF MoS is cheap versus JCDecaux, Lamar and Outfront on cash flow. Net margin is ~6%, ROIC 7% and Altman Z 1.2, with digital and dialog segments adding cyclicality. Price is in the upper part of its range, so it has partly rerated; the discount is partly justified by leverage.
SAX.DE.rationale: Stroeer SE: German out-of-home advertising plus digital and dialog marketing; peers are JCDecaux, Lamar, Outfront, Clear Channel Outdoor.

TFI.PA.relative_comps: Valuation: p_fcf ~14x with DCF/EPV/owner-earnings MoS of roughly 54-62% is cheap against free-to-air peers that trade on 6-9x EV/EBIT, but the multi-method gap partly reflects cash-rich balance sheet and stable TV-ad cash conversion rather than pure mispricing. Growth: revenue -2.5% yoy / -2.9% 3y CAGR and EPS -26% yoy are in line with the structurally declining linear-TV cohort (ITV, M6, ProSieben), not a differentiator. Margins/quality: net margin 6.7%, ROIC ~9%, Altman Z 1.6 are mid-pack for broadcasters; the low reported gross margin is an accounting artifact of content-cost classification. Trend: price sits only ~30% of the way up its 52-wk range and below its 200-day, so the market is pricing continued ad-revenue erosion. Verdict: cheap vs peers, but the discount is largely justified by secular decline; the real mispricing case rests on cash return and the TF1 streaming/Salto exit cleanup.
TFI.PA.rationale: TF1 Group (Paris) is the leading French free-to-air commercial broadcaster (TF1, TMC, TFX, LCI plus TF1+ streaming and Newen studios). True comps are other European free-to-air groups whose economics are national TV-ad share, content amortization and linear decline: M6 (MMT.PA), ITV, Mediaset/MFE, ProSiebenSat.1, RTL Group, Atresmedia.

TTD.relative_comps: Valuation: p_fcf of ~9.5x is extraordinarily low for a 78% gross-margin platform and below ad-tech peers such as Magnite and PubMatic (high-single to low-teens FCF multiples) and far below AppLovin; DCF MoS ~24% and deep-value iv15 MoS ~70% agree, though EPV MoS of -88% shows the price needs growth well beyond steady-state earnings, so the cheapness is conditional on growth holding. Growth: revenue +18% yoy / +22% 3y CAGR leads the independent ad-tech cohort (MGNI, PUBM, CRTO, DV mostly single-digit to mid-teens) but is decelerating against AppLovin's much faster ramp; EPS +17% is only in line. Margins: 79% gross margin is top tier, net margin 15% is solid but ROIC ~7.5% is weak because of goodwill/stock-comp heavy capital base. Trend: price is only ~13% off its 52-wk low with the high near $42 and a 200-day near $19, i.e. in a deep downtrend after the Amazon/Kokai/Ventura competitive-share fears. Verdict: cheap vs peers; the discount is partly justified by walled-garden competition (Amazon DSP, Google, AppLovin) and a decelerating growth story, but the gap to peers on a FCF basis looks larger than the quality gap.
TTD.rationale: The Trade Desk (US) is the largest independent buy-side programmatic demand-side platform (DSP) for open-internet and CTV advertising. True comps are independent ad-tech platforms (Magnite, PubMatic, Criteo, DoubleVerify, IAS), the high-growth mobile ad-tech peer AppLovin, and the walled-garden/retail-media competitors that actually take its share (Alphabet DV360, Amazon DSP).

WPP.L.relative_comps: Valuation: p_fcf ~7x and DCF/EPV/owner-earnings MoS of 45-56% make WPP the cheapest of the big holding groups on cash flow (Publicis, Omnicom-IPG trade at roughly 10-14x FCF), but EPV MoS is only 45% and Graham fails. Growth: revenue -8% yoy and -2% 3y CAGR against Publicis delivering mid-single-digit organic growth, i.e. WPP is the share-loser of the group (account losses, Kantar/WPP Media reset, AI disintermediation fears). Margins: net margin slightly negative and ROIC ~1.8% (impairments, restructuring) versus Publicis/Omnicom ROIC in the teens; Altman Z ~0.9 flags balance-sheet stress not seen at Publicis. Trend: proximity_52wk of 0.95 (measured from the low) puts the shares near the top of a 218-430p range, above the 200-day (~310p), so the stock has already re-rated sharply and the cheapness is no longer accompanied by a downtrend. Verdict: cheap vs peers on cash-flow multiples, but the discount is substantially JUSTIFIED by shrinking revenue, collapsing returns and leverage; the mispricing thesis requires a turnaround, not just mean reversion.
WPP.L.rationale: WPP plc (London) is the second-largest global advertising and communications holding group (WPP Media, Ogilvy, VML, Burson, plus data/production). True comps are the other agency holding groups: Publicis, Omnicom/IPG, Havas, Dentsu, plus smaller listed digital agencies Stagwell, S4 Capital and Next Fifteen.

YELP.relative_comps: Valuation: p_fcf ~4.1x is the lowest in the local-listings/online-marketplace cohort (Tripadvisor, Angi, Cars.com sit around 6-12x FCF) with DCF MoS ~70%, owner-earnings ~40% and iv15 ~63%, though EPV MoS of only 17% shows that flat-earnings value is much closer to price, so the margin of safety depends on FCF being sustainable (heavy stock-comp add-back flatters p_fcf). Growth: revenue +3.7% yoy / +7% 3y CAGR and EPS +19% (buyback-driven) are in line to slightly better than TRIP and ANGI, which are flat or shrinking. Margins: 90% gross margin and ~10% net margin are good, ROIC ~9% is respectable; Altman Z 2.2 is unremarkable. Trend: price is only ~21% up from its 52-wk low and below its 200-day (~$23), a persistent downtrend driven by Google/AI-search disintermediation of local discovery and slowing multi-location ad growth. Verdict: cheap vs peers; the gap is partly justified by the structural dependency on Google traffic and the weak growth runway, but a ~4x FCF multiple with ongoing buybacks looks like an overshoot.
YELP.rationale: Yelp Inc (US) runs a local-business review and advertising marketplace monetized through pay-per-click ads to SMBs and services leads (restaurants, home services). Its true economics resemble other consumer-review/local-lead marketplaces and Google-dependent classified/listing models: Angi, Tripadvisor, Nextdoor, Cars.com, Groupon, with Google Maps/Search as the dominant competitor and traffic gatekeeper.
